info.name: RhythmX V2 API
info.description:
API surface for the RhythmX V2 headless backend (Next.js frontend ↔ PHP JSON API). Draft contract — request/response shapes may still shift during build; this collection is the reference the frontend should code against.

---

## Setup (one minute)

1. Set the **`base_url`** collection variable (defaults to `http://localhost:8000`).
2. Run **Auth › Login** (or Register → Verify email → Login). The login/refresh/social/2FA requests auto-save `access_token` and `refresh_token` into collection variables via test scripts.
3. Every other request inherits **Bearer {{access_token}}** from the collection — nothing to configure per request.
4. On a `401`, run **Auth › Refresh access token** and retry.

## Response envelope (every endpoint)

```json
{
  "status": true,          // false on any error
  "message": "Human-readable summary",
  "data": { },             // payload on success
  "errors": { "field": "reason" },  // 422 only
  "meta": { "pagination": { "page": 1, "size": 20, "total": 132, "pages": 7, "has_next": true, "has_prev": false } }
}
```

## Status codes

`200` OK · `201` created · `202` accepted (async/2FA step) · `400` malformed request · `401` not authenticated · `402` payment required/failed · `403` authenticated but not allowed · `404` not found (also returned for things you don't own) · `409` conflict/duplicate · `410` expired (invites, OTPs) · `422` validation failed (`errors` map) · `429` rate limited (`Retry-After` header) · `500` server error (generic message only).

## Conventions

- IDs in URLs are opaque `reference` strings (`rel_8shd72`), never numeric database ids.
- All timestamps ISO-8601 UTC; money values are **strings** with 2 decimals (`"15.00"`).
- Lists paginate with `?page=&size=` (size clamped to 100).
- Anything priced answers **402 + a payment-init payload** — see the *Payments* folder description for the full checkout flow.
- 🔓 in a request's docs = public (no token) · 🔑 = user token · 📩 = gateway webhook (backend testing only).

## Standard error responses (apply to every request, not repeated per request)

`401` not logged in / token expired (call Auth › Refresh) · `404` not found or not yours · `422` validation failed (`errors` map) · `429` rate limited (`Retry-After`). Request docs list only endpoint-specific responses.

request.description:
Accepts EITHER form:

  {"email": "...", "otp": "483920"}   — the 6-digit code, valid 15 minutes
  {"token": "<from the emailed link>"} — the link, valid 24 hours

Both live on the same record, so using one kills the other. This is what signs the user in: it returns the normal access/refresh tokens.

`next_step` tells the frontend which screen to show — "profile_setup" until the profile is finished, then null.

Path is flat: /api/auth/email-verification-resend.

Always the same reply whether or not the address exists. 60-second cooldown per account; 5 per 5 minutes per IP.

Always the same reply, whether or not the address exists.

What actually gets emailed depends on the account:
  • has a password        → a real reset link
  • no password, email    → the signup code again (resume), NOT a reset link
  • no password, social   → "you signed up with Google, sign in that way"

Reset is never allowed to create a first password, since that would skip profile setup.

The token moved out of the path and into the body.

Single use. On success every existing session for the user is destroyed and a confirmation email is sent. Grants no session of its own — the user logs in again afterwards.
Only used when login returns 202 with a challenge_token, which happens when the account has TOTP enabled. A wrong code does not burn the challenge; it is spent only on success.

item.description:
Signup, login (email + social), token refresh, email verification, password reset, 2FA.

**Token flow:** `Login` returns an access token (~15 min) and a refresh token (~30 days). The requests in this folder auto-save both into collection variables via a test script, so every other request in the collection is authenticated automatically. When you get a `401`, run `Refresh access token` and retry.

In the Next.js app: keep the refresh token in an httpOnly cookie, keep the access token in memory only.

*A folder-level script auto-saves `access_token` / `refresh_token` from any login-style response in this folder into collection variables.*

item.name: Onboarding

request.description:
Where the user is in the wizard. Use `wizard.current_step` and the boolean flags to decide which screen to show on resume.

Also returns `marketing_opt_in` — the user's latest stored answer, or null if they have never been asked — so the profile screen can show the toggle as they left it.

Only **first_name** and **last_name** are required. **phone, gender and dob are OPTIONAL** — omit them, or send `""`, and they are stored as NULL. (Changed 2026-07-27: phone and gender used to be required. Signup must not block on demographics.)

Optional does not mean "anything goes": if you DO send phone or gender they are still validated — phone must match `^\+?[0-9 ()-]{6,20}$`, gender must be `male` or `female`. Send a real value or leave the key out entirely.

⚠️ phone, gender and dob ARE required later at **Account › Update my profile** (`PATCH /api/me`). Onboarding is the only place they can be skipped, so the account edit screen must collect all of them.

This is where an email signup sets its FIRST password — registration no longer takes one, so without this the account can never log in again once its token expires. Send `password` only when the account has no password yet (social signups and returning users omit it).

**There is no `password_confirmation` field** (removed 2026-07-27) — the frontend uses a show-password toggle instead, which serves the same purpose. Password strength rules are unchanged: minimum 8 characters and a zxcvbn score of at least 3. Note that `PATCH /api/auth/password-reset/confirm` still has its own `password_confirmation`.

marketing_opt_in defaults to true when omitted. The answer is written to an append-only consent log with the timestamp, screen and wording version; re-saving the same answer does not add a duplicate row.

The photo is NOT set here — see "Upload avatar", which can run before or after.

POST (was PATCH). One of: artist | collaborator | label.

"collaborator" is stored as account_type "contributor" — the column name predates the UI wording. Both spellings are accepted; the API answers with the stored one.

Changing type after saving type-specific details clears them, so the matching details step must be done again.

Next: whichever of the three account-type detail endpoints matches the choice.

Takes exactly two fields: artist_name and country. Both are required.

country is a two-letter code (NG, GB); it is uppercased before storing, so "ng" is fine. Anything else returns 422.

Replaces the old generic PATCH /account-profile, which no longer exists. Only valid when the chosen account type is artist — a label or collaborator calling this gets 409 naming the type they actually picked.

Genre and the streaming links are no longer part of this step. Any other fields sent are ignored, and values already stored for them are left untouched.

Storage: artist_name goes to users_artist.name, country to users.country — so it comes back as data.user.country in this response and in GET /api/onboarding. There is no second copy on the artist row.

Path changed from /terms to /accept-terms; the old path now returns 404.

Requires the account-type details step to be done first. `accepted` must be exactly true.

Billing cycles: `quarterly` (3 months), `biannual` (6 months) or `annual` (1 year) — **there is no monthly billing**; anything else is a 422. Plan prices are yearly; for sub-yearly cycles the 202 response includes `cycle_price` = (yearly / periods) + the configured surcharge (10% today). Example: Kickstart £19.99/yr → quarterly £5.50, biannual £10.99.

Free plan → 200, wizard completes with an active subscription.
Paid plan → **202** `payment_required: true` with the plan snapshot, `billing_cycle` and `cycle_price`; checkout follows in the Subscriptions API.
Label Master (custom-priced) → **200**, wizard completes with an `on_hold` subscription: the team quotes the label and activates after payment; paid features stay locked until then.

item.name: Account

request.description:
✅ **Live** — implemented and verified 2026-07-28. Updated 2026-07-29: `dial_code` and `phone_number` are **gone** — `phone` is a single free-form value.

One call to boot the whole account area: the person, their plan and their wallet balance.

🔑 Requires `Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}}`. The user always comes from the token — there is no user id in any URL.

### 200 response

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Account.",
  "data": {
    "user": {
      "reference": "ACCT0001",
      "first_name": "Ada",
      "last_name": "Obi",
      "email": "ada@example.com",
      "avatar": "user-abc123.png",
      "avatar_url": "https://.../media/users/avatar/user-abc123.png",
      "account_type": "artist",
      "auth_provider": "email",
      "status": "active",
      "locale": "en",
      "country": "NG",
      "two_factor_enabled": false,
      "created_at": "2026-07-28 08:29:30",
      "phone": "+234 802 940 987",
      "gender": "female",
      "dob": "1990-05-04",
      "timezone": "west-central-africa"
    },
    "subscription": {
      "reference": "...",
      "status": "active",
      "billing_cycle": "monthly",
      "started_at": "...",
      "expires_at": "...",
      "plan": { "id": 2, "name": "Pro" }
    },
    "wallet": { "balance": "0.00" }
  }
}
```

### Three fields decide what you render

| Field | Use it for |
|---|---|
| `account_type` | Which type-profile screen to show — `artist`, `contributor`, `label`, `label_member` |
| `auth_provider` | `google` / `apple` / `microsoft` users have **no password** — hide "current password" fields |
| `subscription` | `null` when nothing is active — show the upgrade prompt |

⚠️ `account_type` is **`contributor`**, not `collaborator`. The URL says `collaborator`, the stored value says `contributor`.

**Use this to prefill the account form.** `phone` is one free-form field, returned exactly as the user saved it — there is no split dial code / number pair any more, so put the whole value into a single phone input.

`two_factor_enabled` is always `false` today — 2FA is not built.

✅ **Live** — implemented and verified 2026-07-28. Updated 2026-07-29: `dial_code` is **gone** — `phone` is a single free-form field, same as onboarding.

Edit the person: names, phone, gender, date of birth.

🔑 Requires `Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}}`. The user always comes from the token — never pass a user id.

**All five are required.** This is the opposite of the onboarding profile step, where phone, gender and dob may be skipped — this screen is where the user fills in whatever they left blank at signup.

⚠️ **Prefill the whole form from `GET /api/me` and show every field.** A user who skipped phone/gender/dob at onboarding cannot make a one-field edit (fixing a typo in their surname, say) without also supplying the missing ones — a partial body returns 422 on fields the user never saw:

```
PATCH /api/me  {"first_name":"Ada","last_name":"Lovelace"}
→ 422 {"errors":{"phone":"Phone number is required.",
                 "gender":"Gender is required.",
                 "dob":"Date of birth is required."}}
```

The Figma frame shows only first name, last name, email and phone — it is **short two fields**. Gender and date of birth need adding to the form.

### Phone is ONE field

Send the whole number in `phone`, exactly as the user typed it — the same shape onboarding takes. A dial code is welcome but never required; nothing is joined, normalised or validated against the countries list any more, and the value is **stored and returned as sent**. If the design still shows a dial-code selector, join selector + number into the single `phone` value client-side before sending.

### Rules

| Field | Rule |
|---|---|
| `first_name`, `last_name` | required, max 100 |
| `phone` | required, matches `^\+?[0-9 ()-]{6,20}$` — digits, spaces, `(` `)` `-`, optional leading `+` |
| `gender` | required, `male` or `female` |
| `dob` | required, `YYYY-MM-DD`, at least 13 years ago |

### Rejected fields

Sending any of `email`, `password`, `account_type`, `status`, `locale`, `referral_code` returns **422** — they are not silently ignored. Email is read-only (contact support); password and timezone have their own endpoints.

### Responses

**200** returns the same `user` object as `GET /api/me`.
**422** `{"status":false,"message":"Validation failed.","errors":{"phone":"..."}}` — keyed by field name. A phone already on another account returns 422 on `phone`.

✅ **Live** — implemented and verified 2026-07-28.

Replace the profile picture. **multipart/form-data**, field name `avatar`.

🔑 Requires `Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}}`.

⚠️ The field is **`avatar`** — an older draft of the docs said `api_upload`, which was never correct.

JPG, PNG or WebP, **2 MB max**.

⚠️ **The file type is checked by reading the image bytes**, not the filename or the `Content-Type` you send — renaming `notes.txt` to `photo.png` is rejected with 422.

The previous avatar file is deleted automatically, so there is no separate "remove avatar" call. Same storage path as the onboarding avatar upload, so the image does not move when it is edited later.

### Responses

**200**

``` json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Avatar uploaded.",
  "data": {
    "avatar": "user-abc123.png",
    "avatar_url": "https://.../media/users/avatar/user-abc123.png"
  }
}

 ```

**422** field missing, file too large, or not a real image.

⏳ **NOT BUILT YET — returns 404 today.** Contract only; the shape may still change. Do not code against this.

Two-step, OTP-confirmed.

| | Step 1 | Step 2 |
|---|---|---|
| Email signup | send current password → verified, OTP emailed | OTP + new password + confirmation |
| Social signup (Google/Microsoft/Apple) | nothing to send → OTP emailed | OTP + new password + confirmation |

**The new password is collected at step 2, not step 1** — nothing unconfirmed is parked server-side between the steps.

Social accounts have no password at all, so check `auth_provider` from `GET /api/me` to decide whether to show the "current password" field.

⚠️ On success **every device is logged out, including the one making the request.** The user signs in again everywhere with the new password.

✅ **Live** — implemented and verified 2026-07-28.

Saves the user's **timezone**.

🔑 Requires `Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}}`.

⚠️ **The screen labelled "Language & Region" is really "Language & Timezone".** The frontend label needs changing.

- The list under "Region" is a **timezone picker**, not a country picker. "Lagos, Nigeria" on the frame should read **"Lagos, West Africa"**.
- This endpoint does **not** touch `users.country`.
- **Language is display-only.** There is no translation capability yet, so show the current value and do not build a switcher.

### The value must be a slug

Send the `slug` from **`GET /api/meta/timezones`** (134 entries of `{slug, text}`):

✅ `west-central-africa`
❌ `Africa/Lagos`
❌ `West Central Africa`

Anything not in that list returns 422.

### Responses

**200**
```json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Timezone updated.",
  "data": { "timezone": "west-central-africa", "language": "en" }
}
```
**422** `{"errors": {"timezone": "That timezone is not recognised."}}`

✅ **Live** — implemented and verified 2026-07-28. ⚠️ **Response simplified 2026-07-31 — see below. The old shape is gone.**

The four notification switches, plus this device's push flag.

🔑 Requires `Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}}`.

**All four keys are always present, in this fixed order**, even for a brand-new account that has never saved anything. There are no seeded rows in the database — the API merges a fixed catalogue with whatever the user has stored and defaults the gaps to on.

### 200 response

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Notification preferences.",
  "data": {
    "preferences": {
      "unusual_activity": true,
      "new_releases": true,
      "updates_announcements": true,
      "new_features": true
    },
    "push_enabled": false
  }
}
```

### What changed on 2026-07-31

The response used to be a nested `sections` → `items` → `channels` structure carrying the card titles, row labels and a per-channel array. **That is removed.** It is now four booleans and a flag. If you bound to `data.sections`, rebind to `data.preferences`.

### Row copy is yours now

The API sends state, not labels. Use these:

| Key | Row on the screen |
|---|---|
| `unusual_activity` | Email me whenever I encounter unusual activity |
| `new_releases` | Email me about my new releases |
| `updates_announcements` | Notify me of important updates and announcements |
| `new_features` | Email me about new features and updates |

Grouping is yours too: the first two sit under **Email Alerts**, the last two under **News Alerts**.

### `push_enabled` is read-only here

It reflects whether **this** device has a live push token. PATCHing this endpoint will not change it — flip it with `POST` / `DELETE /api/me/fcm-tokens`. A device with no token reads `false`, and the push switch should be inert until one is registered.

ℹ️ Behind the scenes each topic still stores four channels (`email`, `push`, `sms`, `whatsapp`). Only `email` has a sender wired to it, so only `email` is surfaced. `sms` carries OTPs only and is never a preference.

✅ **Live** — implemented and verified 2026-07-28. ⚠️ **Simplified 2026-07-31: send a plain boolean per topic.**

Flip the notification switches.

🔑 Requires `Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}}`.

### Body

```json
{ "preferences": { "new_releases": false } }
```

A bare `true` / `false` is the email channel — the only channel anything sends on today.

### Valid topics (exactly these four)

| Key | Row on the screen |
|---|---|
| `unusual_activity` | Email me whenever I encounter unusual activity |
| `new_releases` | Email me about my new releases |
| `updates_announcements` | Notify me of important updates and announcements |
| `new_features` | Email me about new features and updates |

**Partial updates are safe.** Only the topics you actually send are written; anything omitted keeps its current value.

Values must be real booleans — `"true"` and `1` are rejected.

### Push is not here

`push_enabled` in the response is read-only. Turning push on or off is `POST` / `DELETE /api/me/fcm-tokens` — a live token for the device *is* the on state. Sending `push_enabled` in this body does nothing.

### Responses

**200** returns the same shape as the GET:

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Notification preferences updated.",
  "data": {
    "preferences": {
      "unusual_activity": true,
      "new_releases": false,
      "updates_announcements": true,
      "new_features": true
    },
    "push_enabled": false
  }
}
```

**422** unknown topic — `{"preferences": "Unknown topic: releases."}`
**422** non-boolean — `{"preferences.new_releases.email": "Value must be true or false."}`

ℹ️ The older nested form still works — `{"preferences": {"new_releases": {"email": false, "push": true}}}` — for the day `sms` / `whatsapp` get senders. You do not need it today.

❄️ **DEFERRED — not built, returns 404 today.** Proposed only. Do not code against this.

The database columns and the login-side verification step already exist, so login branches on a flag that nothing can currently set. Enabling 2FA is deliberately out of scope for the Account section and will ship with its own endpoints.

`two_factor_enabled` in `GET /api/me` is therefore always `false` today.

❄️ **DEFERRED — not built, returns 404 today.** Proposed only. Do not code against this. See "Enable 2FA".

ℹ️ Note for the Security & Privacy screen: it currently has **no live endpoint at all**. 2FA and passkeys are both deferred, and the "Disable Export" toggle was dropped entirely — nothing is stored for it. Build that screen last.

request.description:
✅ **Live** — implemented and verified 2026-07-28. The two login-path defects that blocked this screen are fixed.

Signed-in devices for the current user, newest login first.

🔑 Requires `Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}}`.

`?search=` filters on device name and maps to the screen's **Search devices** box. Omit it for the full list.

### 200 response

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Devices.",
  "data": {
    "devices": [
      {
        "id": 62,
        "name": "Macintosh",
        "type": "desktop",
        "location": "Ikenne, Nigeria",
        "ip": "105.112.0.1",
        "last_login_at": "2026-07-28 15:01:42",
        "first_seen_at": "2026-07-20 09:14:03",
        "is_current": true
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Reading the fields

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| `is_current` | The device making this request. Render it as "Now" / "This device" and hide its sign-out button — the API returns **409** if you try to sign out the device you're on. |
| `last_login_at` | ⚠️ The Figma column says **"Last Used"** — that label is wrong. It is a last-login time; there is no activity tracking. |
| `first_seen_at` | When this device was first ever seen. Different from `last_login_at`, and the signal a "login from a new device" alert would use. |
| `location` | `city, country`, e.g. `"Lagos, Nigeria"`. **Can be `null`** — the lookup is capped at 2s and skipped for private IPs, so render a fallback rather than assuming a string. |
| `type` | `mobile` · `tablet` · `desktop` · `other` |

One row per **device**, not per login. Logging in repeatedly on the same phone updates that row rather than adding new ones.

✅ **Live** — implemented and verified 2026-07-28.

Signs out one device. `:deviceId` is the numeric `id` from `GET /api/me/devices`.

🔑 Requires `Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}}`.

⚠️ **You cannot sign out the device you are currently using** — that returns **409**. Hide the button on the row where `is_current` is `true`; use `POST /api/auth/logout` for the current session instead.

⚠️ **This also deletes that device's push tokens.** The user chose to sign that device out, so continuing to push to it would be wrong. There is no separate call to make.

The session dies immediately: the opaque Bearer token is resolved through `_session_devices`, so once the row is gone the token stops resolving. Verified — the signed-out device's next request returns 401.

### Responses

**200** `{"status": true, "message": "Device signed out."}`
**404** device does not exist **or is not yours** — deliberately the same answer, so the endpoint cannot be used to probe which device ids exist.
**409** that is your current device.

✅ **Live** — implemented and verified 2026-07-28.

Register or refresh this device's push token.

🔑 Requires `Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}}`.

| Field | Rule |
|---|---|
| `token` | **required**, max 255 |
| `platform` | optional, one of `web` · `android` · `ios` (defaults to `web`) |

**Safe to call on every app start.** `fcm_token` is unique, so re-sending the same token updates the existing row rather than creating a duplicate or returning 409 — verified.

**Multiple live tokens per user is the point.** A phone and a laptop signed in at once should both receive push; this does not replace the user's other tokens.

The token is linked to the device that registered it, which is how signing that device out takes its push with it.

### This is how the "Allow Push Notification" toggle works

There is no `push_enabled` boolean anywhere. **A live token is the on state.**

- **On** → request a token from the SDK, POST it here
- **Off** → `DELETE /api/me/fcm-tokens` with that token
- **Back on** → ask the SDK for a token again; usually silent, since the OS remembers permission was granted

Because tokens are per device, turning push off on the laptop leaves the phone still receiving.

### Responses

**200** `{"status": true, "message": "Push token registered."}`
**422** missing/oversized `token`, or an unknown `platform`.

✅ **Live** — implemented and verified 2026-07-28.

Remove a push token. This is how "turn push off" is implemented.

🔑 Requires `Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}}`.

⚠️ **The URL changed.** This was `DELETE /api/me/fcm-tokens/:id`. It is now `DELETE /api/me/fcm-tokens` with **the token in the body**.

Why: the token is up to 255 characters and contains `:` and `-`, so it does not belong in a URL path. More importantly the client holds a **token string**, never a row id — the Firebase SDK hands the app a token, so requiring a database id would force the client to store something it was never given.

The row is deleted outright. No soft-disable, no tombstone: a dead push token is worthless, and the app simply re-prompts and registers a fresh one.

Deletion is scoped to the signed-in user, so knowing another account's token string is not enough to remove it.

### Responses

**200** `{"status": true, "message": "Push token removed."}` — returned **whether or not a row matched**. The caller's intent ("this device should not receive push") is satisfied either way, and a 404 would leak whether a given token exists.
**422** `token` missing from the body.

ℹ️ Signing a device out already deletes its tokens, so you do not need to call this first.

⏳ **NOT BUILT YET — returns 404 today.** Contract only. Do not code against this.

Two-step, OTP-confirmed soft delete. Step 1 submits the reason and emails a code; step 2 submits the code and the account is switched off immediately. No grace window, no admin approval — but not one click either.

The OTP also solves the social-signup problem: Google/Apple/Microsoft accounts have no password, so a password-only check would leave them unable to ever delete.

### `reason_code` — one of these six

| Code | Shown as |
|---|---|
| `too_expensive` | It costs too much |
| `using_another_service` | I'm moving to another distributor |
| `not_using_it` | I don't use it enough |
| `missing_features` | It's missing features I need |
| `technical_issues` | I ran into too many problems |
| `other` | Something else |

`reason_note` is optional on the five and effectively expected on `other`.

### What "deleted" means

Status becomes `deleted`, sessions and tokens revoked, push tokens deleted, subscription cancelled. **Nothing is destroyed** — the row and everything hanging off it stay, and **the wallet balance is left untouched** deliberately so the money stays auditable.

Afterwards, login returns the ordinary invalid-credentials error rather than "this account was deleted" — that is intentional, so an outsider cannot confirm the address was registered.

request.description:
The **Discography** screen. Paginated; label owners/staff see the whole label catalogue, everyone else their own releases.

**Query:** `page` (default 1) · `limit` (default 20, max 100) · `status` (see below) · `type` (single|ep|album|compilation) · `q` (title search, ≤150 chars).

### The `status` filter — review and delivery are two separate axes

A release that is live on the stores has **still cleared review**, so two of these values deliberately overlap:

| Value | Returns |
|---|---|
| `approved` | Cleared review — **whether or not it has shipped**. Includes releases already live. |
| `distributed` | **Actually live on the DSPs.** Never returns an approved-but-unsent release. |
| `draft`, `pending_review`, `rejected`, `on_hold`, `taken_down` | Exact status match. |

`meta.counts` mirrors these filters exactly, so **every chip lists precisely what it counted**. Because `approved` and `distributed` overlap, **the counts do not sum to the catalogue total** — this is intentional, not a bug. Five submissions where an admin approved four and three of those later shipped read as:

```
"counts": { "draft": 0, "pending_review": 0, "approved": 4,
            "rejected": 1, "distributed": 3, "on_hold": 0, "taken_down": 0 }
```

An account with no releases in a given state simply reads `0` there — if `approved` is `0` but `distributed` is not, nothing is wrong: those releases have shipped and are counted under both.

### Card fields

Each item: `reference, title, type, status, distribution_status, cover_url, genre, sub_genre, is_explicit, is_fast_track, release_date, created_at, artists[] (role main|featured, name, links), tracks_total, platforms[], platforms_total, total_streams`.

**`platforms`** is the store names for the release's chips — **the complete list, already ordered for display**: Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube Music, Amazon Music, Deezer and TikTok lead, everything else follows alphabetically. Render as many as fit and take the overflow count from `platforms_total`; don't re-sort client-side or the recognisable stores stop leading.

```
"platforms": ["Spotify", "Apple Music", "YouTube Music", "Amazon Music", "Deezer", "7digital", ...],
"platforms_total": 19
```

Note releases carry ~19 stores on average and up to 56, so the overflow chip realistically reads "+17 more", not "+3 more".

`meta.pagination` (`page, limit, total, pages, has_next, has_prev`) + `meta.counts` (the per-status chips described above).

All responses use the house envelope `{"status", "message", "data"?, "errors"?, "meta"?}`. Errors: **401** bad/missing token, **404** release/track not found _or not yours_, **422** validation (`errors` maps field → reason), **429** rate limited.

request.description:
The **Release Details** screen: the full record for one release — every scalar field plus `artists[]`, `tracks[]` (each with its own `royalty_splits[]`), `platforms[]`, `links[]` and `status_log[]`.

A submitted release is **read-only** here — the only write it accepts is `POST /api/releases/:reference/takedown`. All the mutable steps live in the draft wizard under `/api/releases/draft/...`.

`:reference` is the release's public handle (`releases.reference`, a 25-char string like `rel_9f3a2b7c4d`) — never the numeric id. Scope comes from the token: a label owner/staff member sees the label's whole catalogue, everyone else only their own releases. A reference that isn't yours answers **404**, never 403 — the endpoint never confirms someone else's release exists.

---

## The one thing to get right: there are FOUR different `status` fields

"status" shows up at four levels, each with its **own** vocabulary. Don't reuse one field's values to interpret another.

| Field | Level | Possible values |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | release — **review outcome** | `draft`, `pending_review`, `approved`, `rejected`, `distributed`\*, `on_hold`, `taken_down` |
| `distribution_status` | release — **delivery to stores** | `not_sent`, `processing`, `live`, `failed`, `takedown_requested`, `takedown_completed` |
| `platforms[].status` | per store | `pending`, `sent`, `live`, `failed` |
| `tracks[].royalty_splits[].status` | per split | `pending`, `accepted`, `rejected` |

**Review outcome and delivery are two separate facts on two separate columns.** A release that is live on Spotify is _still_ `status: "approved"` — `status` does not become "live" or "distributed" when it ships. To answer **"is this out on the stores?"** read `distribution_status === "live"`, not `status`.

\*`distributed` is a **legacy** review value from the old V1 import (a delivery word stranded in the review column). Treat it as read-only and equivalent to `approved` for display. New releases will never move _into_ it — they stay `approved` while `distribution_status` carries the delivery state.

---

## Response shape (`data.release`)

**Scalars**

| Field | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `reference` | string | Public handle, use in all release URLs |
| `title` | string |  |
| `type` | string | `single` |
| `status` | string | Review outcome — see table above |
| `distribution_status` | string | Delivery state — see table above |
| `cover_url` | string | null |
| `genre` | string |  |
| `sub_genre` | string | null |
| `is_explicit` | bool | Release-level advisory flag |
| `is_fast_track` | bool | Fast-track add-on purchased |
| `release_date` | date | `YYYY-MM-DD` |
| `release_time` | time | null |
| `original_release_date` | date | null |
| `language` | string |  |
| `version` | string | null |
| `upc` | string | null |
| `copyright_year` | string |  |
| `copyright_holder` | string |  |
| `all_platform_plays` | int | Lifetime plays across every track and every DSP (the "All Platform plays" header figure), from `streams_platform`. `0` when nothing reported yet |
| `created_at` | datetime |  |
| `updated_at` | datetime |  |

**`artists[]`** — main artist(s) first, then featured. `{ role: "main"｜"featured", name, artist_id (int｜null), spotify_url (｜null), apple_music_url (｜null), image_url (｜null) }`. `artist_id` is null for artists typed in by hand rather than picked from a lookup.

request.description:
`GET /api/releases/{reference}/earnings`

Lifetime earnings for one release, powering the Release Details "Earnings History" panel.

Returns the release-wide totals plus one flat `earnings` list — a row per (platform × track) that the panel renders directly. There are no nested `platforms[]` or `tracks[]` breakdowns.

**Path params**

- `:reference` — the release's public reference string, e.g. `5sgrc6d68hety1n`.
    

**Response** **`data`**

- `reference` (string) — the release reference.
    
- `currency` (string, fixed `"GBP"`) — all amounts render in GBP; money is summed from `revenue_line_items.amount_due` and rounded to 2 decimals in the response (stored precision is `decimal(18,8)`).
    
- `total_earnings` (number) — every platform × track row for this release, summed (not just the rows returned).
    
- `total_streams` (integer) — lifetime units (`units`) summed across the same rows.
    
- `earnings[]` — most-earning-first, up to 50 rows:
    - `platform` (string|null) — DSP display name, e.g. `"Spotify"`. `null` for legacy V1-migrated data, which carries no per-DSP split.
        
    - `icon` (string|null) — DSP icon URL from `revenue_overview.platform_icon_url`. `null` when no icon is present.
        
    - `type` (string) — the release type (`single`/`ep`/`album`/`compilation`), repeated per row (one release ⇒ one type).
        
    - `track` (string|null) — track title from `revenue_line_items.track_title` (or `revenue_overview.name` on the legacy path).
        
    - `amount` (number) — that (platform × track) slice of `amount_due`, rounded to 2 decimals.
        

**Sources** — lifetime figure from `revenue_line_items` matched by `track_id`, then ISRC, then owner-scoped `track_title`; legacy V1 rows (NULL `track_id`/`isrc`) fall back to `revenue_overview` track rows matched by ISRC within the owner's published statements. The fallback returns `platform`/`icon` as `null` — the row is still a track with an amount.

An empty `earnings: []` with zero totals just means no revenue has been imported for this release yet (see the **200 · Empty** example) — render it as "£0.00, no earnings yet", not an error.

**Errors** (all use the house envelope) — `401` bad/missing token · `404` release not found or not yours · `429` rate limited (`Retry-After`).

**Example response (200)**

``` json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Release earnings.",
  "data": {
    "reference": "5sgrc6d68hety1n",
    "currency": "GBP",
    "total_earnings": 2384.00,
    "total_streams": 412903,
    "earnings": [
      { "platform": "Apple Music", "icon": "https://cdn.rhythmxdistro.com/assets/dsp/apple-music.svg", "type": "single", "track": "Sugar", "amount": 0.32 },
      { "platform": "Spotify", "icon": "https://cdn.rhythmxdistro.com/assets/dsp/spotify.svg", "type": "single", "track": "Sugar", "amount": 0.18 },
      { "platform": "Apple Music", "icon": "https://cdn.rhythmxdistro.com/assets/dsp/apple-music.svg", "type": "single", "track": "Someone I Used To Know", "amount": 0.09 }
    ]
  }
}

 ```

`GET /api/releases/{reference}/earnings`

Lifetime earnings for one release, powering the Release Details "Earnings History" panel.

Returns the release-wide totals plus one flat `earnings` list — a row per (platform × track) that the panel renders directly. There are no nested `platforms[]` or `tracks[]` breakdowns.

**Path params**

- `:reference` — the release's public reference string, e.g. `5sgrc6d68hety1n`.
    

**Response** **`data`**

- `reference` (string) — the release reference.
    
- `currency` (string, fixed `"GBP"`) — all amounts render in GBP; money is summed from `revenue_line_items.amount_due` and rounded to 2 decimals in the response (stored precision is `decimal(18,8)`).
    
- `total_earnings` (number) — every platform × track row for this release, summed (not just the rows returned).
    
- `total_streams` (integer) — lifetime units (`units`) summed across the same rows.
    
- `earnings[]` — most-earning-first, up to 50 rows:
    - `platform` (string|null) — DSP display name, e.g. `"Spotify"`. `null` for legacy V1-migrated data, which carries no per-DSP split.
        
    - `icon` (string|null) — DSP icon URL from `revenue_overview.platform_icon_url`. `null` when no icon is present.
        
    - `type` (string) — the release type (`single`/`ep`/`album`/`compilation`), repeated per row (one release ⇒ one type).
        
    - `track` (string|null) — track title from `revenue_line_items.track_title` (or `revenue_overview.name` on the legacy path).
        
    - `amount` (number) — that (platform × track) slice of `amount_due`, rounded to 2 decimals.

**201** → request filed (`distribution_status` becomes `takedown_requested`, ops process it).

**409** → not a live release, already requested, or already taken down.
**403** → label staff without the `release.delete` permission.

All responses use the house envelope `{"status", "message", "data"?, "errors"?, "meta"?}`. Errors: **401** bad/missing token, **404** release/track not found *or not yours*, **422** validation (`errors` maps field → reason), **429** rate limited.

request.description:
`POST /api/releases/draft`

**Step 1 of the wizard — always first.** Creates the draft and returns its `reference`; every other wizard call keys on that reference, so store it. You do **not** send the whole release here — just the basics, then fill the other steps with their own endpoints (see the folder description for the end-to-end flow).

Requires an artist profile on the account (finish onboarding first — otherwise **409**). Label staff need the `release.add` permission.

#### Request payload — `application/json`

- `title` (string, **required**) — release title, 1–255 chars. e.g. `"Midnight Sun"`
    
- `type` (string, **required**) — one of `single` · `ep` · `album` · `compilation` (lowercase).
    
- `language` (string, optional) — slug from `GET /api/meta/languages`. e.g. `"english"`
    
- `genre` (string, optional) — slug from `GET /api/meta/genres`. e.g. `"pop"`
    
- `sub_genre` (string, optional) — slug that must belong to the chosen `genre`.
    
- `version` (string, optional) — e.g. `"Deluxe Edition"`, ≤150 chars.
    
- `release_date` (string, optional) — `YYYY-MM-DD`. **Defaults to today** if omitted.
    
- `original_release_date` (string, optional) — `YYYY-MM-DD`, for re-releases. Empty string clears it.
    
- `release_time` (string, optional) — `HH:MM` 24-hour, e.g. `"00:00"`. Empty string clears it.
    
- `upc` (string, optional) — barcode, 12–14 digits. Leave out to have one assigned.
    
- `copyright_year` (string, optional) — 4-digit year. Defaults to the current year.
    
- `copyright_holder` (string, optional) — ≤150 chars. e.g. `"Sony Music"`
    
- `is_explicit` (0/1, optional) — release-level explicit flag.
    

Everything optional here can also be set later via `PATCH /api/releases/draft/{reference}` — same fields, same rules.

#### Response `data`

- `reference` (string) — the draft's public id, e.g. `"REL7K2M9QX4TBWH01"`. **Every later wizard call needs it.**
    
- `status` (string) — always `"draft"`.
    

#### Errors

`401` · Not authenticated · `403` · Label staff without `release.add` · `409` · No artist profile yet — finish onboarding first · `422` · Validation failed — field errors in `errors` · `429` · Rate limited

``` json
{
  "status": false,
  "message": "Validation failed.",
  "errors": {
    "title": "Give this release a title (up to 255 characters).",
    "type": "Type must be single, ep, album or compilation."
  }
}

 ```

#### Example response — 201

``` json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Draft created.",
  "data": { "reference": "REL7K2M9QX4TBWH01", "status": "draft" }
}

 ```

response.name: 201 · Draft created

request.description:
`PATCH /api/releases/draft/{reference}`

**Partial update** of the Release Details step. Send **only the fields you're changing** — anything you leave out is untouched. Sending an empty body is a 422. Draft-only: after submit every field is locked and this answers **409**.

#### Path params

- `:reference` — the draft's reference from `POST /api/releases/draft`. e.g. `REL7K2M9QX4TBWH01`
    

#### Request payload — `application/json` (all fields optional, send ≥1)

- `title` (string) — 1–255 chars.
    
- `type` (string) — `single` · `ep` · `album` · `compilation`.
    
- `language` (string) — slug from `GET /api/meta/languages`.
    
- `genre` (string) — slug from `GET /api/meta/genres`.
    
- `sub_genre` (string) — must belong to the chosen `genre`. Empty string clears it.
    
- `version` (string) — ≤150 chars. Empty string clears it.
    
- `release_date` (string) — `YYYY-MM-DD`.
    
- `original_release_date` (string) — `YYYY-MM-DD`. Empty string clears it.
    
- `release_time` (string) — `HH:MM` 24-hour. Empty string clears it.
    
- `upc` (string) — 12–14 digits. Empty string clears it (one gets assigned).
    
- `copyright_year` (string) — 4-digit year.
    
- `copyright_holder` (string) — ≤150 chars.
    
- `is_explicit` (0/1) — release-level explicit flag.
    

#### Response `data`

- `reference` (string) — the draft's reference.
    
- `updated` (array of strings) — the field names that were actually saved, e.g. `["release_date", "copyright_year"]`.
    

#### Errors

`401` · Not authenticated · `403` · Label staff without `release.edit` · `404` · Release not found or not yours · `409` · Already submitted — drafts only; use the takedown flow · `422` · Validation failed (or empty body — `errors.body`) · `429` · Rate limited

``` json
{
  "status": false,
  "message": "Validation failed.",
  "errors": { "release_date": "Use the YYYY-MM-DD date format." }
}

 ```

#### Example response — 200

``` json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Draft updated.",
  "data": {
    "reference": "REL7K2M9QX4TBWH01",
    "updated": ["release_date", "release_time", "copyright_year", "copyright_holder"]
  }
}

 ```

`DELETE /api/releases/draft/{reference}`

Deletes the draft **and everything attached to it**: tracks (audio files included), contributors, royalty splits, artists, platform selections and the cover image. There is no undo. Only drafts can be deleted — a submitted release answers **409** and goes through the takedown flow instead. Label staff need `release.delete`.

#### Path params

- `:reference` — the draft's reference. e.g. `REL7K2M9QX4TBWH01`

No request body. No `data` in the response.

#### Errors

`401` · Not authenticated · `403` · Label staff without `release.delete` · `404` · Release not found or not yours · `409` · Already submitted — cannot delete; request a takedown · `429` · Rate limited

#### Example response — 200

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Draft deleted."
}
```

request.description:
`POST /api/releases/draft/{reference}/artwork`

Uploads the cover for the Release Details step. Uploading again **replaces** the previous cover — no separate delete call. The file's real bytes are checked, not its filename, so a renamed WebP still fails. Draft-only: after submit this answers **409**.

#### Path params

- `:reference` — the draft's reference. e.g. `REL7K2M9QX4TBWH01`

#### Request payload — `multipart/form-data`

- `artwork` (file, **required**) — the cover image. Rules, all enforced:
  - **JPG or PNG** only.
  - **Square** — width must equal height exactly.
  - **At least 1400×1400 px** (3000×3000 recommended — DSPs ask for it).
  - **10 MB max.**

That's the whole payload — one file field named `artwork`, nothing else.

#### Response `data`

- `cover_url` (string) — public URL of the stored cover, e.g. `"https://rhythmxdistro.cc/upload/music/cover/cover-x8k2m4p7q9w3e5r7t9y2.jpg"`. Show it in the wizard immediately.

#### Errors

`401` · Not authenticated · `403` · Label staff without `release.edit` · `404` · Release not found or not yours · `409` · Already submitted · `422` · Bad file — reason in `errors.artwork` (missing file, too big, wrong format, not square / too small; the message includes your actual dimensions) · `429` · Rate limited (uploads have their own tighter limit) · `500` · Storage failed — retry

```json
{
  "status": false,
  "message": "Validation failed.",
  "errors": {
    "artwork": "Cover art must be square and at least 1400 x 1400 pixels (yours is 1200 x 800)."
  }
}
```

#### Example response — 200

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Cover artwork uploaded.",
  "data": {
    "cover_url": "https://rhythmxdistro.cc/upload/music/cover/cover-x8k2m4p7q9w3e5r7t9y2.jpg"
  }
}
```

request.description:
`GET /api/releases/draft/{reference}/tracks`

Lists every track on the draft in upload order — the Tracks step's list view. Also the way to get a **fresh signed** **`audio_url`** for playback (they expire).

#### Path params

- `:reference` — the draft's reference. e.g. `REL7K2M9QX4TBWH01`
    

No request body.

#### Response `data`

- `tracks` (array) — one object per track, same shape as the add-track response:
    - `reference` (string) — the `trackRef` for PATCH / DELETE / contributors / splits.
        
    - `order` (int) — tracklist position.
        
    - `title` · `language` · `isrc` · `version` · `lyrics` — `null` when unset.
        
    - `is_explicit` · `has_advisory` (bool).
        
    - `audio_url` (string) — signed, expiring playback URL.
        
    - `uploaded_at` (string) — datetime.
        

An empty draft returns `"tracks": []` — valid, just means nothing uploaded yet.

request.description:
`POST /api/releases/draft/{reference}/tracks`

Adds one track: the **audio file and its metadata go in the same multipart request** — there is no separate "save metadata" call. Call this once per track. `PATCH .../tracks/{trackRef}` is only for editing a track that already exists. Max **50 tracks** per release. Draft-only: after submit this answers **409**.

#### Path params

- `:reference` — the draft's reference. e.g. `REL7K2M9QX4TBWH01`
    

#### Request payload — `multipart/form-data`

- `audio` (file, **required**) — the master. **WAV, FLAC or MP3** (sniffed from the bytes), **200 MB max**. One request per file — no chunking.
    
- `title` (text, **required**) — track title, 1–255 chars.
    
- `language` (text, optional) — slug from `GET /api/meta/languages`. **Defaults to the release's language** if omitted.
    
- `isrc` (text, optional) — format `CC-XXX-YY-NNNNN`, dashes/spaces ignored, e.g. `GBABC2512345`. **Leave blank to have one assigned** — most artists should.
    
- `version` (text, optional) — e.g. `"Acoustic"`, ≤100 chars.
    
- `lyrics` (text, optional) — plain text, ≤20,000 chars.
    
- `is_explicit` (text `0`/`1`, optional) — explicit lyrics flag.
    
- `has_advisory` (text `0`/`1`, optional) — parental-advisory flag.
    

#### Response `data`

- `track` (object):
    - `reference` (string) — **this is the** **`trackRef`** for contributors, splits, PATCH and DELETE. Store it.
        
    - `order` (int) — position in the tracklist, assigned by upload order.
        
    - `title` · `language` · `isrc` · `version` · `lyrics` — as saved (`isrc`/`version`/`lyrics` are `null` when unset).
        
    - `is_explicit` · `has_advisory` (bool).
        
    - `audio_url` (string) — **signed, expiring** playback URL. Don't persist it; re-fetch the track list when you need a fresh one.
        
    - `uploaded_at` (string) — datetime.
        

#### Errors

`401` · Not authenticated · `403` · Label staff without `release.edit` · `404` · Release not found or not yours · `409` · Already submitted, **or** the 50-track cap is hit · `422` · Validation failed — reasons keyed by field (`audio`, `title`, `isrc`…) · `429` · Rate limited (upload limit) · `500` · Storage failed — retry

``` json
{
  "status": false,
  "message": "Validation failed.",
  "errors": {
    "title": "Give this track a title (up to 255 characters).",
    "audio": "Attach the audio file (field name `audio`)."
  }
}

 ```

#### Example response — 201

``` json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Track uploaded.",
  "data": {
    "track": {
      "reference": "TRK4H8N2WQ7XKMV93",
      "order": 1,
      "title": "Midnight Sun",
      "language": "english",
      "isrc": null,
      "version": null,
      "is_explicit": false,
      "has_advisory": false,
      "lyrics": null,
      "audio_url": "https://rhythmxdistro.cc/media/tracks/track-p2m9x4k7...?sig=…&exp=…",
      "uploaded_at": "2026-08-03 11:24:05"
    }
  }
}

 ```

originalRequest.description:
`POST /api/releases/draft/{reference}/tracks`

Adds one track: the **audio file and its metadata go in the same multipart request** — there is no separate "save metadata" call. Call this once per track. `PATCH .../tracks/{trackRef}` is only for editing a track that already exists. Max **50 tracks** per release. Draft-only: after submit this answers **409**.

#### Path params

- `:reference` — the draft's reference. e.g. `REL7K2M9QX4TBWH01`
    

#### Request payload — `multipart/form-data`

- `audio` (file, **required**) — the master. **WAV, FLAC or MP3** (sniffed from the bytes), **200 MB max**. One request per file — no chunking.
    
- `title` (text, **required**) — track title, 1–255 chars.
    
- `language` (text, optional) — slug from `GET /api/meta/languages`. **Defaults to the release's language** if omitted.
    
- `isrc` (text, optional) — format `CC-XXX-YY-NNNNN`, dashes/spaces ignored, e.g. `GBABC2512345`. **Leave blank to have one assigned** — most artists should.
    
- `version` (text, optional) — e.g. `"Acoustic"`, ≤100 chars.
    
- `lyrics` (text, optional) — plain text, ≤20,000 chars.
    
- `is_explicit` (text `0`/`1`, optional) — explicit lyrics flag.
    
- `has_advisory` (text `0`/`1`, optional) — parental-advisory flag.
    

#### Response `data`

- `track` (object):
    - `reference` (string) — **this is the** **`trackRef`** for contributors, splits, PATCH and DELETE. Store it.
        
    - `order` (int) — position in the tracklist, assigned by upload order.
        
    - `title` · `language` · `isrc` · `version` · `lyrics` — as saved (`isrc`/`version`/`lyrics` are `null` when unset).
        
    - `is_explicit` · `has_advisory` (bool).
        
    - `audio_url` (string) — **signed, expiring** playback URL. Don't persist it; re-fetch the track list when you need a fresh one.
        
    - `uploaded_at` (string) — datetime.
        

#### Errors

`401` · Not authenticated · `403` · Label staff without `release.edit` · `404` · Release not found or not yours · `409` · Already submitted, **or** the 50-track cap is hit · `422` · Validation failed — reasons keyed by field (`audio`, `title`, `isrc`…) · `429` · Rate limited (upload limit) · `500` · Storage failed — retry

``` json
{
  "status": false,
  "message": "Validation failed.",
  "errors": {
    "title": "Give this track a title (up to 255 characters).",
    "audio": "Attach the audio file (field name `audio`)."
  }
}

 ```

#### Example response — 201

``` json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Track uploaded.",
  "data": {
    "track": {
      "reference": "TRK4H8N2WQ7XKMV93",
      "order": 1,
      "title": "Midnight Sun",
      "language": "english",
      "isrc": null,
      "version": null,
      "is_explicit": false,
      "has_advisory": false,
      "lyrics": null,
      "audio_url": "https://rhythmxdistro.cc/media/tracks/track-p2m9x4k7...?sig=…&exp=…",
      "uploaded_at": "2026-08-03 11:24:05"
    }
  }
}

 ```

request.description:

#### Path params

- `:reference` — the draft's reference. e.g. `REL7K2M9QX4TBWH01`
- `:trackRef` — the track's `reference` from the add-track response. e.g. `TRK4H8N2WQ7XKMV93`

- `language` (string) — slug from `GET /api/meta/languages`.

request.description:
`DELETE /api/releases/draft/{reference}/tracks/{trackRef}`

Removes the track **and everything on it**: the audio file, its contributor credits and its royalty splits. No undo. This is also how you **replace a track's audio** — delete, then `POST .../tracks` again (a new `trackRef` is minted, so re-save contributors/splits after). Draft-only: after submit this answers **409**.

#### Path params

- `:reference` — the draft's reference. e.g. `REL7K2M9QX4TBWH01`
- `:trackRef` — the track's reference. e.g. `TRK4H8N2WQ7XKMV93`

No request body. No `data` in the response.

#### Errors

`401` · Not authenticated · `403` · Label staff without `release.edit` · `404` · Release **or track** not found or not yours · `409` · Already submitted · `429` · Rate limited

#### Example response — 200

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Track removed."
```
```json
}
```

request.description:
`PUT /api/releases/draft/{reference}/tracks/{trackRef}/royalty-splits`

The Split Royalty step, **per track**. **Replace-all**: the array you send becomes the track's complete split list. Two hard rules:

1. Percentages must sum to **exactly 100** (±0.01) — include **your own share** as one of the rows.
2. `{"splits": []}` (empty array) **clears** all splits — you keep 100%. That's valid and is also the default: a track with no splits passes the checklist.

Optional step — only tracks that *have* splits are checked at submit. Max **20 splits per track**. Draft-only: after submit this answers **409**.

#### Path params

- `:reference` — the draft's reference. e.g. `REL7K2M9QX4TBWH01`
- `:trackRef` — the track's reference. e.g. `TRK4H8N2WQ7XKMV93`

#### Request payload — `application/json`

- `splits` (array, **required** — may be empty to clear) — each item:
  - `name` (string, **required**) — collaborator's name, 1–255 chars.
  - `percent` (number, **required**) — their share, 0.01–100. Up to 2 decimal places.
  - `email` (string, optional) — how the split gets linked to a person (see below). Omit for a name-only record.
  - `role` (string, optional) — free text ≤100 chars, defaults to `"Collaborator"`.

#### What the email does

- Matches a **RhythmX account** → the split links to that user immediately, stored `pending` — they must accept it from their invitations list. **Your own email auto-accepts** (no self-invitation).
- No account yet → stored as an **external** recipient. Not a dead end: at **submit** (not here) they get one invite email with a 7-day sign-up link; once they register and accept, they're paid directly.
- No email at all → a name-only record; it can never be accepted or paid until an email is added.

#### Response `data`

- `splits` (array) — the saved rows: `name`, `email` (or `null`), `percent` (2 dp), `role`, `status` (`accepted` for your own row, `pending` for everyone else).

#### Errors

`401` · Not authenticated · `403` · Label staff without `release.edit` · `404` · Release **or track** not found or not yours · `409` · Already submitted · `422` · Validation failed — bad rows use dotted keys (`splits.0.percent`); a bad total keys on `splits` and tells you your sum · `429` · Rate limited

```json
{
  "status": false,
  "message": "Validation failed.",
  "errors": {
    "splits": "Split percentages must add up to exactly 100 (yours total 95)."
  }
}
```

#### Example response — 200

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Royalty splits saved.",
  "data": {
    "splits": [
      { "name": "Mike Ross", "email": "mike@example.com", "percent": 10, "role": "Collaborator", "status": "pending" },
      { "name": "Elena Godson", "email": null, "percent": 30, "role": "Collaborator", "status": "pending" },
      { "name": "Me", "email": "me@example.com", "percent": 60, "role": "Collaborator", "status": "accepted" }
    ]
  }
}
```

response.name: 200 · Splits saved (own row auto-accepts)

request.description:
`GET /api/releases/draft/{reference}/artists`

The Artist step's saved state: who is on the release, grouped `main` / `featured`. Both arrays are empty on a fresh draft.

#### Path params

- `:reference` — the draft's reference. e.g. `REL7K2M9QX4TBWH01`

No request body.

#### Response `data`

The Choose Platforms step. **Replace-all**: the ids you send become the complete DSP selection — to add one store, send the full list including it. At least one id is required. Draft-only: after submit this answers **409**.

``` json

  "status": false,
  "message": "Validation failed.",
  "errors": {
    "platform_ids": "Unknown or inactive platform ids: 99, 120. Use GET /api/meta/platforms."
  }
}

 ```

#### Example response — 200

``` json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Platforms saved.",
  "data": { "platform_ids": [1, 7, 9] }
}

 ```

request.description:
`POST /api/releases/draft/{reference}/submit`

The final step: moves the draft to **`pending_review`**. **No request body.** After this the release is read-only — every `/draft/...` endpoint answers 409, and the only remaining mutation is the takedown flow.

**When to enable the Submit button:** `GET .../progress` runs exactly this checklist, so once it returns `ready_to_submit: true`, this call passes validation.

#### Path params

- `:reference` — the draft's reference. e.g. `REL7K2M9QX4TBWH01`

#### What happens on success

- Status: `draft` → `pending_review`; the plan snapshot is re-captured **at submit time** (an artist who upgraded mid-wizard submits on the new plan).
- The "we received your release" email is queued (artist or label variant).
- Every royalty-split collaborator **without a RhythmX account** gets their invite email now — one per address, 7-day sign-up link. This is the only moment those go out.

#### Free-plan fee gate (402)

A free account gets **1** included release; drafts never count, only submitted ones. Past that, each submit costs **GBP 5** pay-as-you-go. Until Payments ships, that path answers **402** and **nothing is submitted**:

```json
{
  "status": false,
  "message": "Your free plan covers 1 release. Each release after that costs GBP 5.00. ...",
  "data": {
    "fee": { "amount": 5, "currency": "GBP", "reason": "payg_release" },
    "payment": null
  }
}
```

`payment` will carry the gateway init once Payments exists — treat non-null as "send the user to pay, then retry submit". Paid plans skip this gate entirely.

#### Response `data`

- `reference` (string) — the release's reference.
- `status` (string) — always `"pending_review"`.

#### Errors

`401` · Not authenticated · `402` · Free-plan PAYG fee due — nothing submitted (`data.fee` above) · `403` · Label staff without `release.edit` · `404` · Release not found or not yours · `409` · Already submitted · `422` · Checklist incomplete — one `errors` entry **per missing step**, same keys as `progress`, so you can jump the user straight to the step · `429` · Rate limited

```json
{
  "status": false,
  "message": "This release is not ready to submit yet.",
  "errors": {
    "release_details": "Add the title, genre, language and cover artwork.",
    "release_date": "Set the release date."
  }
}
```

#### Example response — 200

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Release submitted for review.",
  "data": { "reference": "REL7K2M9QX4TBWH01", "status": "pending_review" }
}
```

response.name: 200 · Submitted for review

Royalty splits you have **accepted** — your share of other people's releases. This is the read side of the wizard's Split Royalty step: where `PUT /api/releases/draft/{reference}/tracks/{trackRef}/royalty-splits` writes the splits on *your* release, this lists the ones other people put *your* name on.

Pending ones are not here — see `GET /api/royalty-split/invitations`.

Paginated with `?page=` and `?limit=` (limit clamped to 100), newest first. `meta.pagination` carries `page/limit/total/pages/has_next/has_prev`.

Each split item carries enough context to recognise it without a second call:

```json
{
  "id": 4821,
  "percent": 25.0,
  "role": "Producer",
  "status": "pending",
  "name": "Ada Made",
  "email": "ada@example.com",
  "invited_at": "2026-07-14 10:22:03",
  "answered_at": null,
  "track":   { "reference": "...", "title": "Sunrise", "isrc": "GBABC2512345" },
  "release": { "reference": "...", "title": "Sunrise EP", "type": "ep",
               "status": "distributed", "release_date": "2026-09-15",
               "cover_url": "https://.../cover-x.jpg", "artist": "Kolade" },
  "invited_by": "Narkz Ent"
}
```

`id` is the `release_royalty` row id — it is what `PATCH .../invitations/{id}` takes. `invited_by` is the label when the release belongs to one, otherwise the uploading account. `answered_at` is `null` while the split is still pending.

**Scope.** These rows live on releases you do *not* own, so nothing here uses catalogue scoping — every query is keyed on your own user id. A split id belonging to someone else answers **404**, never 403, so the endpoint never confirms that another user's split exists.

request.description:
Splits **waiting on your answer** — the invitations inbox.

A split lands here when someone building a release adds a collaborator whose email matches your account; the wizard links it to your user id and stores it `pending`. The release owner's own row is written `accepted` and never appears as an invitation.

`meta.pending` is the total count — use it for the nav badge (it is the unpaginated total, so it stays correct on page 2). Same pagination and item shape as `GET /api/royalty-split`.

**Splits addressed to an email with no RhythmX account appear here too — after that person registers.** They are stored with `user_id` NULL, emailed once when the release is submitted, and linked to the new account when its email is verified. They arrive still `pending`, because owning the mailbox is not the same as agreeing to the share — the person accepts here themselves.

An unanswered invite is closed by the expiry sweep after 7 days and the artist is notified, but **expiry never voids the split**: the row stays `pending` with `user_id` NULL, so a later signup still links it and it still shows up here.

**Scope.** These rows live on releases you do *not* own, so nothing here uses catalogue scoping — every query is keyed on your own user id. A split id belonging to someone else answers **404**, never 403, so the endpoint never confirms that another user's split exists.

Statuses: **200** OK, **401** bad/missing token, **429** rate limited.

All responses use the house envelope `{"status", "message", "data"?, "errors"?, "meta"?}`.

request.description:
Answer a split invitation. `{id}` is the `release_royalty` row id from the invitations list.

Body takes the **target state**, not a toggle:

```json
{ "status": "accepted" }
```

`status` must be `accepted` or `rejected`; anything else is **422**.

Only your own **pending** rows can be answered — answering one twice returns **409** naming what you already chose. The write itself is guarded on `status = 'pending'`, so two simultaneous answers cannot both win.

The response returns the updated split in the same shape as the list endpoints, with `answered_at` filled in.

**What rejecting does — and deliberately does not do.** It records your answer and sends the release owner an in-app notification (no email). It does **not** rebalance the track's remaining splits back to 100%: silently moving other people's percentages is not a decision this endpoint makes. That is intentional and settled, not a gap — the declaration invariant (the wizard demands exactly 100) and the payout invariant are separate on purpose. Only `accepted` splits are ever paid; everything else, including a rejection that lands after the release is live, goes to the release owner.

**Accepting late does not backdate.** You earn from the next revenue import onward, never retroactively.

**Scope.** These rows live on releases you do *not* own, so nothing here uses catalogue scoping — every query is keyed on your own user id. A split id belonging to someone else answers **404**, never 403, so the endpoint never confirms that another user's split exists.

Statuses: **200** answered, **401** bad/missing token, **404** not found or not yours, **409** already answered, **422** bad or missing `status`, **429** rate limited.

All responses use the house envelope `{"status", "message", "data"?, "errors"?, "meta"?}`.

item.description:
The release catalogue and the release wizard (tasks/04-releases.md).

**How it fits together:** `POST /api/releases/draft` creates a draft and returns its `reference`. Every wizard step (details, artwork, tracks, contributors, splits, artists, platforms) saves into that draft under `/api/releases/draft/{reference}/...`, and `GET .../progress` tells you which Figma step to show next. Once submitted the release becomes **read-only**: the plain `/api/releases/...` endpoints are the Discography / Release-Details screens, and the only mutation left is `POST .../takedown`.

---

### Create a release — call by call

You do **not** send one big payload. Save a draft first, then push each screen as the user finishes it. The draft holds everything on the server between steps, so the user can leave and come back.

**1. Create the draft** — `POST /api/releases/draft` with `title` + `type`. Returns `reference`. Store it — every later call needs it. (An account with no artist profile gets **409**: finish onboarding first.)

**2. Fill the rest — in any order.** Each of these is independent, so fire them as the user completes each screen, or all at once at the end. Nothing here has to run in sequence:
- **Details** → `PATCH /draft/{reference}` — genre, language, dates, copyright, etc. Partial: send only what changed.
- **Cover** → `POST /draft/{reference}/artwork` — multipart, field `artwork`.
- **Each track** → `POST /draft/{reference}/tracks` — multipart: the audio file **and** its metadata (title, ISRC, lyrics…) go in the *same* request. There is no separate "save track metadata" call; `PATCH .../tracks/{trackRef}` is only for editing a track you already uploaded.
- **Per track (optional)** → `PUT .../tracks/{trackRef}/contributors` and `PUT .../tracks/{trackRef}/royalty-splits`. These need the `trackRef` the upload returned, so they come after that track exists.
- **Artists** → `PUT /draft/{reference}/artists` — at least one `main`.
- **Platforms** → `PUT /draft/{reference}/platforms`.

**3. Check readiness** — `GET /draft/{reference}/progress` returns a per-step checklist, the first incomplete step (`current_step`), a `percent`, and `ready_to_submit`. Drive the wizard's step highlighting and the Submit button off this — don't compute it yourself.

**4. Submit** — `POST /draft/{reference}/submit`. Runs the same checklist; if anything is missing it answers **422** with one `errors` entry per incomplete step (same keys as `progress`), so you can jump the user straight back. On success the release moves to `pending_review`.

**Order rules in one line:** only step 1 must go first (it mints the `reference`); everything in step 2 is independent and safe to parallelize; splits/contributors follow their track's upload because they need its `trackRef`.

**Splits gotcha:** royalty splits are per **track** and must sum to **exactly 100** — or be empty, which means you keep 100%. See "Set royalty splits" for how external collaborators get invited at submit.

**Editing vs. submitted:** every `/draft/...` write requires the release to still be a draft. After submit they all answer **409** — a live release changes only through `POST .../takedown`.

---

### Response envelope — every endpoint, success AND error

Every response uses the same wrapper:

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Human-readable summary you can show the user",
  "data": { "...": "the payload; on lists also data.meta.pagination" },
  "errors": { "field_name": "why that field failed" }
}
```

- **`status`** — boolean. `true` on success, `false` on every error. (It is **not** the string `"success"`/`"error"`.)
- **`message`** — human-readable; safe to surface in the UI.
- **`data`** — the payload. **Omitted entirely when empty** (the key is absent, not `null`). List endpoints nest pagination at `data.meta.pagination`; some also add `data.meta.counts` or `data.meta.pending`.
- **`errors`** — appears **only on `422` validation**. It is an **object** mapping each bad field to a plain reason — e.g. `{ "title": "Give this release a title.", "type": "Type must be single, ep, album or compilation." }`. **A required field you left out of the payload shows up here by its name.** Nested items use dotted keys, e.g. `"splits.0.percent"`. On success and on non-422 errors this key is **absent** — those carry their reason in `message` only.

**Status codes used in this folder:**
- **200 / 201** — success.
- **401** — missing/invalid token. `message` only.
- **402** — payment required. `data.fee` = `{amount, currency, reason?}`, `data.payment` = `null` until Payments ships. A non-null `payment` later means "send the user to pay, then retry".
- **403** — label staff without the required permission. `message` only.
- **404** — not found *or not yours* (same response either way — no existence leak). `message` only.
- **409** — conflict: already submitted / already answered / duplicate. `message` only.
- **422** — validation failed. `errors` object populated.
- **429** — rate limited. `message` only, plus a `Retry-After` header.

Each request below carries its own success example and at least one error example under the **Examples** dropdown.

---

**Scope:** a label owner or staff member operates on the label's whole catalogue; everyone else on their own releases. The label is derived from the token, never sent by the client.

**Auth:** every route needs the Bearer token. Writes are rate-limited per user (`api_write`, uploads `api_upload`), reads `api_read`.

Entries marked **[coming]** are designed but not yet live — do not bind them.

item.name: Label

request.description:
🔑 **Auth required.**

The label organisation — details, head-counts, and what **you** are allowed to do.

`/api/me` is the person; this is the organisation. The label is resolved from your token, never from the URL, so one label can never read another's.

### Who can call anything under /api/label

| Caller | Access |
|---|---|
| **Label owner** (`label.user_id`) | Everything, ungated |
| **Staff** (`account_type: label_member` on the team) | Reads open; each write checks their role's permission |
| **Roster artist** | `403` — being signed to a label does not make you an operator of it |
| Anyone else | `403` |

### Response

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Label.",
  "data": {
    "label": {
      "reference": "LBL7Q2M4XK9P1AB",
      "name": "Wave Records",
      "slug": "wave-records",
      "email": "hello@waverecords.com",
      "phone": "+2348011111111",
      "region": "NG",
      "website": "https://waverecords.com",
      "logo": "label-q8zzm5vtc9w91e1e.jpg",
      "logo_url": "https://api.rhythmx.com/upload/label/label-q8zzm5vtc9w91e1e.jpg",
      "is_verified": false,
      "wallet_control": "shared",
      "created_at": "2026-03-14 09:22:01"
    },
    "counts": { "artists": 12, "team": 3, "roles": 3 },
    "access": {
      "is_owner": true,
      "role": "Owner",
      "permissions": { "release.add": true, "team.create": true, "...": "all 21 keys" }
    }
  }
}
```

### Notes for the frontend

- **`access.permissions` is the caller's own effective permission map** — 21 keys, every one present, `true`/`false`. Use it to hide or disable buttons instead of letting the user click and get a 403. The owner gets every key `true` and `role: "Owner"` (they sit on no role).
- `logo` / `logo_url` are `null` until a logo is uploaded.
- `wallet_control` (`shared` | `label_full`) is **read-only here** — it decides whether roster artists may withdraw their own money and is changed from the withdrawal settings, not this screen.
- `counts` drives the dashboard tiles without three extra list calls.

### Endpoint-specific responses

`403` — you are not a label owner or staff member.

request.description:
🔑 **Auth required — owner only.**

Edit the label's own details. **Staff always get `403` here**, whatever their role: these are the organisation's identity fields and the permission catalogue has no key for them.

### Body — send only what changed

All five fields are optional; send at least one or you get a `422`.

| Field | Rules |
|---|---|
| `name` | 1–250 chars. Changing it **regenerates `slug`** automatically. |
| `email` | Valid address. This is the label's contact email, *not* the owner's login. |
| `phone` | Free-form, max 25 chars. Send `""` to clear it. |
| `region` | ISO-2 country code, uppercase (`NG`, `GB`). **Cannot be cleared** — required at onboarding since 2026-07-27. |
| `website` | Full URL, max 200 chars. Send `""` to clear it. |

`label_name` is accepted as an alias for `name`, and `country` for `region`, matching onboarding.

### Rejected fields → 422

Sending any of these is an error, not a silent drop, so you never believe a change saved when it didn't:

`slug` · `reference` · `is_verified` · `logo` · `user_id` · `wallet_control`

- **`slug`** follows `name`. It is unique across all labels — if "Wave Records" is taken you get `wave-records-1`. Read it back from the response.
- **`logo`** → use `POST /api/label/logo`.
- **`wallet_control`** → changed from the withdrawal settings, not here. It decides whether roster artists may withdraw their own money.

### Response

`200` with the full refreshed `data.label`, same shape as `GET /api/label`. Re-read `slug` from it after a rename.

### Endpoint-specific responses

`403` — you are staff, not the owner.
`422` — validation, a rejected field, or an empty body.
