request.description:
🔑 **Auth required.** Open to the owner and any staff member — no permission key needed to read the roster.

The artists signed to your label, newest first.

### Query

| Param | Notes |
|---|---|
| `page` | 1-based, default `1` |
| `limit` | default `20`, **max 100** (clamped, not rejected) |
| `search` | optional; matches first name, last name, `"first last"`, stage name, email or phone |

⚠️ **This list uses `limit`, not `size`.** The collection description mentions `?page=&size=` — that is out of date for this folder.

### Response

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Artists.",
  "data": {
    "artists": [
      {
        "reference": "0SVP5KC2A2RALZR",
        "first_name": "Tolu",
        "last_name": "Bello",
        "stage_name": "Tolu B",
        "email": "tolu@example.com",
        "phone": null,
        "genre": "Afrobeats",
        "avatar_url": "https://api.rhythmx.com/upload/users/avatar/user.png",
        "portrait_url": null,
        "status": "active",
        "joined_at": "2026-05-02 11:04:19"
      }
    ]
  },
  "meta": {
    "pagination": { "page": 1, "limit": 20, "total": 12, "pages": 1, "has_next": false, "has_prev": true }
  }
}
```

### Notes for the frontend

- **`reference` is the person's `users.reference`** — that is what every `/api/label/artists/{reference}` route takes. `label_members` has no reference column of its own.
- **`avatar_url` vs `portrait_url`**: `avatar` is the account photo (always present, falls back to the default `user.png`); `portrait` is the artist press photo and is often `null`. For a roster card, prefer `portrait_url` and fall back to `avatar_url`.
- `stage_name` and `genre` come from the artist profile and are `null` if they never completed it.
- `status` is the **user account** status (`active`, `pending`, `suspended`), not a roster status. There is no per-label enable/disable yet.
- An empty page returns `artists: []` with `total: 0` — a `200`, never a `404`.

🔑 **Auth required.** Open to the owner and any staff member.

One artist on your roster.

### Path

`:reference` — the person's **`users.reference`** (e.g. `0SVP5KC2A2RALZR`), exactly as returned by the roster list. Not a numeric id.

### Response

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Artist.",
  "data": {
    "artist": {
      "reference": "0SVP5KC2A2RALZR",
      "first_name": "Tolu",
      "last_name": "Bello",
      "stage_name": "Tolu B",
      "email": "tolu@example.com",
      "phone": null,
      "gender": null,
      "dob": null,
      "genre": "Afrobeats",
      "bio": "Lagos-born singer…",
      "avatar_url": "https://api.rhythmx.com/upload/users/avatar/user.png",
      "portrait_url": null,
      "spotify_url": null,
      "apple_music_url": null,
      "is_verified": false,
      "status": "active",
      "joined_at": "2026-05-02 11:04:19",
      "registered_at": "2026-04-28 08:15:33"
    }
  }
}
```

### Notes for the frontend

- **No plays, earnings or releases here — on purpose.** The Figma artist profile aggregates all three, but that data belongs to the Analytics, Earnings and Releases sections. Call those with the artist's reference rather than having this endpoint duplicate them.
- `joined_at` = when they joined **this label**. `registered_at` = when their account was created. They differ for an artist who signed up alone and joined later.
- `is_verified` is the **artist profile** verification badge, not the label's `is_verified`.
- An artist on a *different* label answers `404`, identical to one that does not exist — you cannot use this to probe which references are real.

### Endpoint-specific responses

`404` — not on your roster (or no such artist).

🔑 **Auth required.** Permission: **`artist.delete`** (owner always allowed).

Removes the artist from your label. Immediate — there is no request/approval flow, matching the plain "Are you sure…" confirm dialog in Figma.

### What actually happens

**Only the membership is deleted.** The artist keeps:

- their user account and login,
- their releases,
- their wallet and earnings,
- their artist profile.

They are simply no longer signed to you. This is *not* an account deletion, and it is not reversible from this endpoint — re-adding them means sending a fresh invite.

### Response

```json
{ "status": true, "message": "Artist removed from the label." }
```

### Endpoint-specific responses

`403` — your role lacks `artist.delete`.
`404` — not on your roster.

🔑 **Auth required.** Permission: **`artist.invite`** (owner always allowed).

Invites one or more artists to join your roster. Each gets an email with a link.

> ⚠️ **Path changed.** This was `POST /api/label/artist-invitations`. It is now `POST /api/label/artists/invite`.

### Body

Either a list:

```json
{ "emails": ["one@example.com", "two@example.com"] }
```

…or a single comma-separated string, matching the Figma input that accepts several addresses at once:

```json
{ "emails": "one@example.com, two@example.com" }
```

`email` (singular) is accepted as an alias. **Max 25 addresses per call.** Duplicates within one request are collapsed.

### Partial success is normal — read both arrays

One bad address does **not** throw away the rest of the batch:

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "1 invite(s) sent.",
  "data": {
    "sent": [ { "invite_id": 10, "email": "one@example.com" } ],
    "skipped": [
      { "email": "two@example.com", "reason": "An invite is already pending for this address." },
      { "email": "not-an-email",    "reason": "That is not a valid email address." }
    ]
  }
}
```

- **`201`** if at least one invite was sent (even with skips) — show `skipped` as warnings, not as a failure.
- **`422`** if *every* address was skipped. Same body shape, `sent` is empty.

### Skip reasons — show `reason` verbatim

| Reason | Meaning |
|---|---|
| That is not a valid email address. | Failed format check |
| An invite is already pending for this address. | Still open and unexpired — cancel it first to re-send |
| This person is already on your label. | Already yours, artist or staff |
| Sorry, this artist cannot be invited because it's already assigned or belongs to another label on RhythmX Distro. | **Signed to a different label** |

### One artist, one label

An artist can only be signed to one label at a time. The check runs **here** so you find out before an email goes out — and **again when they accept**, because the two can be days apart and they may have joined someone else in between. Acceptance answers `409` with the same wording.

The other label is deliberately never named — that would leak which label a given email records for.

### Invite lifetime

Invites expire after **7 days**. An expired one cannot be accepted — send a new invite rather than trying to extend it.

### The artist's side

The emailed link goes to `/invitations/{token}`, served by **Preview invitation** and **Accept invitation** in this folder. Both are live: an invite can now be completed end to end.

### Endpoint-specific responses

`201` — one or more sent.
`403` — your role lacks `artist.invite`.
`422` — nothing sent: empty body, over 25 addresses, or every address skipped.

request.description:
🔑 **Auth required.** Open to the owner and any staff member.

Your label's staff, newest first.

> ⚠️ **Path changed.** This was `/api/label/team-members`. It is now **`/api/label/team`** — same for every team route in this folder.

### Query

| Param | Notes |
|---|---|
| `page` | 1-based, default `1` |
| `limit` | default `20`, **max 100** (clamped) |
| `search` | optional; matches name, `"first last"`, email or phone |

### Response

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Team.",
  "data": {
    "team": [
      {
        "reference": "R5IVCFUA0CP34O8",
        "first_name": "Ada",
        "last_name": "Obi",
        "email": "ada@example.com",
        "phone": "+2348022222222",
        "avatar_url": "https://api.rhythmx.com/upload/users/avatar/user.png",
        "status": "active",
        "joined_at": "2026-07-29 04:23:46",
        "role": { "id": 1, "name": "A&R Manager" }
      }
    ]
  },
  "meta": {
    "pagination": { "page": 1, "limit": 20, "total": 3, "pages": 1, "has_next": false, "has_prev": false }
  }
}
```

### Notes for the frontend

- **The owner is not in this list.** They have no `label_members` row — they *are* the label. Only staff appear here.
- `role` is the summary only. For the full permission map of a member, call the details endpoint.
- `reference` is the person's `users.reference` and is what every `/api/label/team/{reference}` route takes.
- `status` is the account status. A member removed from the team is set to `suspended`, but they also lose their membership row, so they disappear from this list entirely.

🔑 **Auth required.** Open to the owner and any staff member.

One staff member, **with their full permission map** — this is what the View/Edit Team modal reads.

> ⚠️ **Path changed** from `/api/label/team-members/{reference}`.

### Path

`:reference` — the person's `users.reference` from the team list.

### Response

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Team member.",
  "data": {
    "member": {
      "reference": "R5IVCFUA0CP34O8",
      "first_name": "Ada",
      "last_name": "Obi",
      "email": "ada@example.com",
      "phone": "+2348022222222",
      "avatar_url": "https://api.rhythmx.com/upload/users/avatar/user.png",
      "status": "active",
      "joined_at": "2026-07-29 04:23:46",
      "role": { "id": 1, "name": "A&R Manager" },
      "permissions": {
        "release.add": false, "release.edit": false, "release.delete": false,
        "artist.invite": true, "artist.edit": true, "artist.delete": false,
        "analytics.streams": true, "analytics.earnings": false,
        "analytics.growth": false, "analytics.world": false,
        "earning.stats": false, "earning.export": false,
        "wallet.withdraw": false, "wallet.report_transactions": false,
        "wallet.update_account": false, "wallet.make_payment": false,
        "team.create": true, "team.edit": false, "team.delete": false,
        "role.create": false, "role.update": false
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Notes for the frontend

- **`permissions` is read-only here and belongs to the member's *role*, not the member.** There are no per-person overrides. To change what they can do, either move them to another role (`PATCH /api/label/team/{reference}` with a new `role_id`) or edit the role itself (`PATCH /api/label/roles/{id}`) — which affects everyone on it.
- All 21 keys are always present, `true`/`false`. Never assume a missing key means `false`; it should never be missing.
- Password is never returned, in any form.

### Endpoint-specific responses

`404` — not on your team.

🔑 **Auth required.** Permission: **`team.create`** (owner always allowed).

> 🚨 **This is no longer an invite.** The old `POST /api/label/team-member-invitations` is gone. The label **creates the account outright** and sets the password itself, matching the Figma "New Team" modal.

The member does not accept anything, does not pick an account type, and does not go through onboarding. The account is live the moment this returns.

### Body

| Field | Required | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `first_name` | ✅ | 1–100 chars |
| `last_name` | ✅ | 1–100 chars |
| `email` | ✅ | Valid, and **not already used by any account** |
| `password` | ✅ | Min 8 chars **and** must pass a strength check |
| `password_confirmation` | — | If sent, must match `password` |
| `role_id` | ✅ | An **active** role on *your* label (from `GET /api/label/roles`) |
| `phone` | — | Max 20 chars |

> ⚠️ **The Figma modal has no email field, but email is required** — it is the login. The design needs one added.

**Password strength**: 8 chars is the floor, not the bar. A weak password is rejected with specific guidance, e.g. `"Password is too weak. Add special characters for better security. Use both upper and lower case letters."` Show that message verbatim.

### What gets created

- `account_type: label_member`, `status: active`
- Email marked verified and the onboarding wizard marked complete — staff have no account type to choose and no plan to buy
- A team membership on the role you gave

### The password is not emailed

The member gets an email saying an account was created for them and to sign in — but **the password is deliberately not in it**. Hand it over yourself. The email tells them to change it once they are in. There is no forced password change on first login.

### Response — `201`

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Team member created.",
  "data": {
    "member": {
      "reference": "R5IVCFUA0CP34O8",
      "first_name": "Ada",
      "last_name": "Obi",
      "email": "ada@example.com",
      "phone": "+2348022222222",
      "avatar_url": "https://api.rhythmx.com/upload/users/avatar/user.png",
      "status": "active",
      "role": { "id": 1, "name": "A&R Manager" }
    }
  }
}
```

No photo is uploaded here — the modal's photo goes through `POST /api/label/team/{reference}/avatar` after this returns.

### Endpoint-specific responses

`201` — created.
`403` — your role lacks `team.create`.
`422` — validation. Common: `email` already in use, `password` too weak, `role_id` missing / not yours / deactivated.

🔑 **Auth required.** Permission: **`team.edit`** (owner always allowed).

Edit a staff member's details, move them to another role, or reset their password.

> ⚠️ **Replaces the old "Change team member role"** (`PATCH /api/label/team-members/{reference}`), which only did the role. This does name, phone, role and password.

**`PUT` works identically** — the same handler is mounted on both verbs. `PATCH` is the house style; `PUT` is accepted because the endpoint list specified it.

### Body — send only what changed

Everything is optional, but send at least one field or you get a `422`.

| Field | Rules |
|---|---|
| `first_name` | 1–100 chars |
| `last_name` | 1–100 chars |
| `phone` | Max 20 chars. Send `""` to clear it. |
| `role_id` | An **active** role on your label |
| `password` | Min 8 chars + strength check. **Omit it entirely to leave the password alone** — sending `""` is treated as "no change", not "blank the password". |
| `password_confirmation` | If sent, must match `password` |

### Rejected fields → 422

`email` · `reference` · `account_type` · `status`

**Email cannot be changed here.** It is the login, and moving it needs the same care as changing an artist's identity. There is no endpoint for it yet — support handles it.

### Response

`200` with the **full member object including the refreshed `permissions` map** — identical shape to `GET /api/label/team/{reference}`. After a role change, read `permissions` straight from this response; no second call needed.

### Endpoint-specific responses

`403` — your role lacks `team.edit`.
`404` — not on your team.
`422` — validation, a rejected field, an empty body, or a `role_id` that is not yours / is deactivated.

🔑 **Auth required.** Permission: **`team.delete`** (owner always allowed).

Removes a staff member from your label.

> ⚠️ **Path changed** from `/api/label/team-members/{reference}`.

### What actually happens

Two things, in one transaction:

1. The team membership row is **deleted**.
2. If the account is a `label_member`, its status is set to **`suspended`** — so they can no longer sign in.

A `label_member` account exists only to work for its label. Deleting just the membership would leave a live login answering to nobody, which is why the account is suspended too.

**Nothing is destroyed and it is reversible** — the user row, and everything attached to it, stays. Restoring access means an admin un-suspending the account and re-adding the membership; there is no endpoint for that yet.

### You cannot remove yourself

A staff member calling this on their own reference gets `409` — otherwise they could lock themselves out mid-session:

```json
{ "status": false, "message": "You cannot remove yourself from the team." }
```

The owner is never in the team list, so this cannot be used on them at all.

### Response

```json
{ "status": true, "message": "Team member removed." }
```

### Endpoint-specific responses

`403` — your role lacks `team.delete`.
`404` — not on your team.
`409` — that reference is you.

🔑 **Auth required.** Open to the owner and any staff member.

Everything the Roles & Permission screen needs, in **one call**: your roles with member counts, plus the full catalogue of grantable permissions.

Not paginated. Active roles first, then deactivated, each alphabetical.

### Response

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Roles.",
  "data": {
    "roles": [
      {
        "id": 1,
        "name": "Manager",
        "slug": "manager",
        "description": "Runs the label day to day — releases, roster and reporting.",
        "is_active": true,
        "members": 2,
        "permissions": { "release.add": true, "team.create": false, "...": "all 21 keys" },
        "created_at": "2026-07-29 05:10:44"
      }
    ],
    "catalogue": [
      {
        "key": "discography",
        "label": "Discography",
        "description": "Creating and managing releases on behalf of the label.",
        "permissions": [
          { "key": "release.add",    "label": "Add Release",    "description": "Upload and submit new releases for the label." },
          { "key": "release.edit",   "label": "Edit Release",   "description": "Change the details of a release that already exists." },
          { "key": "release.delete", "label": "Delete Release", "description": "Take a release down and remove it from the catalogue." }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### `catalogue` — draw the toggles from this, never hard-code them

**7 groups, 21 permissions**, in display order, each with a human label and helper text. It is served from the database, so wording can change without a frontend release — render whatever comes back rather than keeping your own copy of the list.

| Group | Permissions |
|---|---|
| Discography | `release.add` `release.edit` `release.delete` |
| Artists | `artist.invite` `artist.edit` `artist.delete` |
| Trends & Analytics | `analytics.streams` `analytics.earnings` `analytics.growth` `analytics.world` |
| Earnings & Royalties | `earning.stats` `earning.export` |
| Wallet | `wallet.withdraw` `wallet.report_transactions` `wallet.update_account` `wallet.make_payment` |
| Team | `team.create` `team.edit` `team.delete` |
| Roles & Permission | `role.create` `role.update` |

### Notes for the frontend

- **Every label starts with three roles** — Manager, A&R and Accountant — seeded on signup. They are starting points: rename, retoggle or deactivate them freely. None of them grants `role.*` or `team.*`.
- Each role's `permissions` map carries **all 21 keys** as `true`/`false`, so you can bind toggles directly without merging against the catalogue.
- `members` is the live count on that role. It is what blocks deactivation — see the Deactivate role request.
- A permission switched off in the catalogue by an admin **disappears from both `catalogue` and every role's `permissions` map**, and stops granting. Do not treat a missing key as a bug.

### Endpoint-specific responses

`403` — you are not a label owner or staff member.

🔑 **Auth required.** Permission: **`role.create`** (owner always allowed).

The "New Role +" button. Creates a role and its permission set in one call.

### Body

| Field | Required | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | ✅ | 1–150 chars. The `slug` is generated from it and made unique within your label — `"A&R Manager"` → `a-r-manager`, and a second one becomes `a-r-manager-1`. |
| `description` | — | Free text, shown under the role name |
| `permissions` | — | Keys to grant. Omit or send `[]` for a role that can do nothing yet. |

### `permissions` accepts either shape

A flat list of granted keys:

```json
{ "permissions": ["artist.invite", "team.create"] }
```

…or the toggle map the panel holds in state, where only `true` entries are kept:

```json
{ "permissions": { "artist.invite": true, "team.create": true, "release.add": false } }
```

**Every key must exist in the catalogue.** An unknown one is a `422` naming it — never a silent drop:

```json
{ "status": false, "message": "Validation failed.",
  "errors": { "permissions": "Unknown permission(s): made.up." } }
```

### One key is added for you

Granting **any** `analytics.*` toggle also stores `analytics.view` behind the scenes. That is the key the Analytics module checks; it is never shown as its own switch and you never send it. You will not see it in the `permissions` map that comes back.

### Response — `201`

The created role, same shape as a row in `GET /api/label/roles` — `id`, `slug`, `is_active: true`, `members: 0`, and the full 21-key `permissions` map.

### Endpoint-specific responses

`201` — created.
`403` — your role lacks `role.create`.
`422` — missing/too-long `name`, or an unknown permission key.

🔑 **Auth required.** Permission: **`role.update`** (owner always allowed).

Rename a role, reword it, retoggle its permissions, or reactivate it.

### Path

`:id` — `label_roles.id`, a plain integer from the roles list. A role belonging to another label answers `404`, not `403`.

### Body — send only what changed

| Field | Rules |
|---|---|
| `name` | 1–150 chars. Changing it **regenerates `slug`**. |
| `description` | Free text. Send `""` to clear it. |
| `permissions` | See below |
| `is_active` | `true` to reactivate a deactivated role. Use `DELETE` to deactivate. |

Send at least one, or `422`.

### ⚠️ `permissions` REPLACES the whole set — it is not a merge

Whatever you send becomes the role's complete permission list. Anything omitted is **revoked**.

```json
{ "permissions": ["artist.invite"] }
```

…leaves the role with `artist.invite` and nothing else, even if it previously had ten.

**Always send the full toggle state from the panel, not just the switches the user touched.** To leave permissions untouched, omit the `permissions` key entirely.

Both shapes are accepted, same as Create role — a flat list, or a `{key: bool}` map where only `true` survives. Unknown keys are a `422` naming them.

### Effect is immediate and applies to everyone on the role

Permissions live on the role, not the person. Every staff member assigned to it gains or loses access on their **next request** — no re-login. Check `members` before saving so you know how many people you are about to affect.

`analytics.view` is still derived automatically from any `analytics.*` key.

### Response

`200` with the refreshed role, including the recalculated `members` count and the full 21-key map.

### Endpoint-specific responses

`403` — your role lacks `role.update`.
`404` — no such role on your label.
`422` — validation, empty body, or an unknown permission key.

🔑 **Auth required.** Permission: **`role.update`** — the same key that edits roles. There is no separate delete permission in the catalogue.

### It deactivates. It never deletes.

The role is flagged `is_active: false` and stays in the list, greyed out. `label_members.role_id` has no null state, so hard-deleting a role would leave staff pointing at a row that no longer exists.

**To bring it back:** `PATCH /api/label/roles/{id}` with `{ "is_active": true }`. Its permissions were never touched, so everyone on it is restored exactly as before.

### A role with members is refused — 409

```json
{ "status": false, "message": "Move the 2 member(s) on this role to another role first." }
```

Check `members` on the roles list and either hide or disable the button when it is above zero. Move each person with `PATCH /api/label/team/{reference}` → `role_id`, then retry.

### Already deactivated → 200, not an error

Calling this twice is safe. The second call returns `200` with `"Role is already deactivated."` and the unchanged role, so a double-click cannot produce a scary error.

### Response

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Role deactivated.",
  "data": { "role": { "id": 1, "name": "A&R Lead", "is_active": false, "members": 0, "...": "" } }
}
```

### Endpoint-specific responses

`200` — deactivated, or already was.
`403` — your role lacks `role.update`.
`404` — no such role on your label.
`409` — the role still has members.

🔓 **Public — no token needed.** ✅ Live.

The invite landing page: "{Label} invited you", shown before the artist commits to anything.

### Path

`:token` — the 48-character hex token from the invite email link (`/invitations/{token}`). The route only matches 32–64 hex chars; anything else falls through to the JSON 404.

### Response

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Invitation.",
  "data": {
    "label": { "name": "Wave Records", "logo_url": null },
    "email": "one@example.com",
    "status": "pending",
    "expires_at": "2026-08-05 06:59:50",
    "account_exists": false
  }
}
```

### `account_exists` decides which form you render

| Value | What the accept page should show |
|---|---|
| `false` | **Create account** — first name, last name, password, terms checkbox |
| `true` | **Sign in** — that email already has an account and must prove it's them |

### Notes for the frontend

- **Only a live, pending invite returns `200`.** Anything else is an error status with a message written for the artist to read — render it as-is:
  - already accepted → `409`
  - cancelled by the label → `410`
  - past its 7 days → `410`
- **Expiry is judged against the clock**, not the stored status, because nothing sweeps the table. Don't compare `expires_at` yourself.
- `email` is the address the invite was sent to. Show it so the artist knows which account they'll be joining with.
- `logo_url` is `null` when the label has not uploaded a logo.

### Endpoint-specific responses

`200` — valid and pending.
`404` — unknown token.
`409` — already accepted.
`410` — cancelled, expired, or the label no longer exists.
`429` — rate limited (50 per 5 min per IP).

✅ Live. Joins the artist to the label's roster and closes the invite.

**Two different flows behind one URL.** Read `account_exists` from the preview call first — it tells you which one you're in.

---

## A · No account yet — 🔓 public, this creates one

Send the body above. No `Authorization` header.

| Field | Required | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `first_name` | ✅ | 1–100 chars |
| `last_name` | ✅ | 1–100 chars |
| `password` | ✅ | Min 8 chars **and** a strength check |
| `accepted_terms` | ✅ | Must be `true` |
| `artist_name` | — | Stage name, max 150. **Defaults to their real name** if omitted |
| `password_confirmation` | — | If sent, must match |

The account is created as `artist` / `active`, with **email already verified and onboarding skipped** — the invite link arriving at that address is the proof of control, and a label artist has no account type to pick and no plan to buy. They land on the dashboard, not the wizard (`next_step` is `null` at login).

**Response carries `data.tokens`** — save them exactly as you do after login and the artist is signed in immediately:

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "You have joined Wave Records.",
  "data": {
    "label": { "reference": "LBL…", "name": "Wave Records", "logo_url": null },
    "user":  { "reference": "0LACCBLXZRVIFTF", "account_type": "artist", "…": "" },
    "tokens": { "access_token": "…", "refresh_token": "…", "token_type": "Bearer", "expires_in": 86400 }
  }
}
```

---

## B · Account already exists — 🔑 Bearer token required

Body is ignored. Send the invited user's `Authorization: Bearer` header.

**Without a token you get `401` plus a flag, not a dead end:**

```json
{
  "status": false,
  "message": "Sign in to accept this invitation.",
  "data": { "sign_in_required": true, "email": "one@example.com" }
}
```

Send them to login (prefill that email), then retry the same token.

**With the wrong account's token → `403`**, naming the address they need. A link alone must never attach someone else's account to a label — a forwarded email or a shared screenshot would otherwise be enough.

**No `tokens` are returned in this flow** — they already have a live session.

---

### One artist, one label

An artist signed to another label is refused with **`409`**:

```json
{ "status": false,
  "message": "Sorry, this artist cannot be invited because it's already assigned or belongs to another label on RhythmX Distro." }
```

This is checked **twice** — when the invite is sent, and again here, because the two can be days apart and the artist may have joined someone else in between. They must leave their current label first.

A `label` or `label_member` account also cannot join a roster (`409`).

### If the session can't be issued

You still get `201`, with `"You have joined {Label}. Please sign in to continue."` and no `tokens`. The join succeeded; only auto-sign-in failed. Send them to login — do **not** retry the token, it is spent.

### Endpoint-specific responses

`201` — joined.
`401` — account exists and you sent no token (see `sign_in_required`), or the token is invalid.
`403` — the token belongs to a different account, or the account is suspended.
`404` — unknown token.
`409` — already accepted, already signed to a label, or a label account.
`410` — cancelled or expired.
`422` — validation on the create path (weak password, terms not accepted, missing name).
`429` — rate limited. Everyone pays 50 per 5 min per IP; the account-creating path also pays 5 per 10 min.

🔑 **Auth required — owner only.** Staff get `403`.

Multipart upload, field name **`logo`**. Replaces the current logo; the old file is deleted from disk.

### Rules

- **JPG, PNG or WebP only.** The type is read from the file's actual bytes, not its name or its `Content-Type` header — renaming `evil.php` to `logo.png` is rejected.
- **Max 2 MB.**
- Do **not** set `Content-Type` yourself. Let the browser/Postman set the multipart boundary.

### Response

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Logo uploaded.",
  "data": {
    "logo": "label-xme6b98z9q1fksl4xh1j.png",
    "logo_url": "https://api.rhythmx.com/upload/label/label-xme6b98z9q1fksl4xh1j.png"
  }
}
```

The filename is randomly generated, so **the URL changes on every upload** — always use the returned `logo_url` rather than caching the old one.

Same storage path as the onboarding logo step, so an image uploaded during signup does not move when it is replaced here.

### Endpoint-specific responses

`403` — you are staff, not the owner.
`422` — no file, upload incomplete, over 2 MB, or not a real JPG/PNG/WebP.
`500` — the file could not be written to disk.

request.description:
🔑 **Auth required.** Open to the owner and any staff member.

Every artist invite this label has ever sent, newest first — pending and accepted together, so the label sees both at a glance.

**Not paginated.** The full list comes back in one call.

### Query

`status` — optional, one of `pending` · `accepted` · `expired` · `revoked`. Anything else is a `422`. Omit for all.

### Response

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Invites.",
  "data": {
    "invites": [
      {
        "invite_id": 10,
        "email": "one@example.com",
        "status": "pending",
        "expires_at": "2026-08-05 04:24:29",
        "accepted_at": null,
        "created_at": "2026-07-29 04:24:29",
        "can_cancel": true
      }
    ]
  },
  "meta": {
    "counts": { "pending": 2, "accepted": 5, "expired": 1, "revoked": 3 }
  }
}
```

### Notes for the frontend

- **Expiry is computed on read, not swept by a cron.** A row still stored as `pending` whose `expires_at` has passed is reported to you as **`expired`**. Trust the `status` field; do not compare `expires_at` yourself.
- **`can_cancel` is the answer to "show the Cancel button?"** — it is `true` only for genuinely pending invites. Saves you re-implementing the expiry rule.
- `meta.counts` always carries all four keys (zeros included) and reflects the **filtered** result when `?status=` is set — use it for tab badges on an unfiltered call.
- `invite_id` is a plain integer, and it is what the cancel endpoint takes. It is *not* a `reference` string like the rest of the API.
- Invites live **7 days**.

### Endpoint-specific responses

`422` — unrecognised `status` value.

🔑 **Auth required.** Permission: **`artist.invite`** (owner always allowed) — the same key that creates invites.

Cancels a still-pending invite. The row is marked `revoked`, not deleted, so it stays visible in the invite list with its history.

### Path

`:invite_id` — the **integer** `invite_id` from the invite list. Not a `reference` string.

### Only pending invites can be cancelled

Check `can_cancel` on the list row before showing the button. Anything else answers `409` naming the current state:

```json
{ "status": false, "message": "Only a pending invite can be cancelled. This one is revoked." }
```

That includes an invite whose 7 days have run out — it reads as `expired`, so cancelling is refused. There is nothing to cancel; just send a new invite.

### Response

```json
{ "status": true, "message": "Invite cancelled." }
```

### Endpoint-specific responses

`403` — your role lacks `artist.invite`.
`404` — no such invite on your label. An invite belonging to another label answers `404` too.
`409` — already accepted, revoked, or expired.

item.description:
Label accounts only — other account types get `403` on this whole group.

**Authorization inside:** the requester must be the label **owner**, or a team member whose role permissions allow the action. Team members can upload releases for label artists; **only the owner can withdraw** (see the Withdrawals folder's `artist_reference`). The owner can never be removed or demoted.

*A folder-level script auto-saves `access_token` / `refresh_token` from any login-style response in this folder into collection variables.*

item.name: Subscriptions

request.description:
🔓 Public — no token. The pricing table, safe to call from a logged-out marketing page.

Returns every active plan with its **feature matrix** and the price of *one billing period* on each cycle. Plan prices are stored yearly; `cycle_prices` applies the sub-yearly surcharge so annual stays the best deal.

`features[].value` is typed per feature — `true`/`false`, a number (`2` artists), or a label (`"72 Hours"`, `"Unlimited"`).

`is_custom: true` (Label Master) means the price is indicative only — the team quotes it. Selecting it puts the subscription `on_hold` rather than starting a checkout.

**200** `{plans: [{id, name, slug, description, price, currency, cycle_prices: {quarterly, biannual, annual}, royalty_commission, max_artists, is_custom, features: [{name, value}]}]}`

🔑 The customer's current plan, when it next bills, and the plan timeline.

Falls back to the **most recent** subscription when none is active, so cancelled and expired states stay visible instead of vanishing. A user who has never subscribed gets **200** with `subscription: null` — an empty state is not an error.

`next_billing_at` is only set when the subscription is genuinely renewing (active *and* `auto_renew`); a cancelled one just runs out at `end_at`, so it returns `null`.

`amount_paid` is the canonical GBP price; `amount` + `currency` are what was actually charged.

**200** `{subscription: {reference, status, billing_cycle, auto_renew, start_at, end_at, next_billing_at, cancelled_at, amount_paid, amount, currency, gateway, plan: {id, name, slug, price, max_artists}} | null, history: [{plan_id, plan_name, action, amount_paid, amount, currency, created_at}]}`

🔑 Starts a first-time paid subscription. Creates a pending `payments` row and a Flutterwave order — redirect the customer to the returned `payment_link`.

`currency` defaults to GBP; any supported currency is accepted. The record keeps **both** figures: `amount_gbp` (e.g. 19.99, the canonical plan price) and `amount` + `currency` + `fx_rate` (what was actually charged, e.g. ₦36,999.95). Re-posting the same checkout within an hour reuses the pending order rather than minting another.

Already subscribed? This returns **409** — use the upgrade endpoint instead (not built yet).

**200** `{reference, payment_link, amount, currency, amount_gbp, fx_rate, gateway}` · **409** already actively subscribed · **422** validation · **502** gateway error · **503** FX provider down.

Next: send the customer to `payment_link`, then call `POST /api/payments/{reference}/verification` when they return.

🔑 Stops the renewal. **Access is not revoked** — the plan runs to `end_at`, which is what the customer already paid for. `status` flips to `cancelled`, `auto_renew` to 0, and a `cancelled` row is written to the history in the same transaction.

`reason` is optional (max 500 chars) and is stored for churn analysis.

Cancelling the **free plan** returns **409** — there is no renewal to stop, and cancelling would only strip access for nothing.

**200** `{subscription: {...}}` (same shape as *Get my subscription*) · **404** no active subscription · **409** free plan · **422** reason too long.

⏳ **NOT BUILT YET — returns 404 today.** Contract only. Do not build against this.

Invite the shared member on a Rhythm Elite plan.

🔑 Requires `Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}}`.

### ⚠️ The path is changing

This request is `POST /api/subscription/member-invitations`. The 2026-07-28 draft renames it to **`POST /api/subscription/members-invite`** — action verbs in the path rather than resources. Confirm before wiring; one of the two will 404.

There is also a third endpoint planned that this collection does not have: **`GET /api/subscription/members`**, returning owner + member with role, status and `joined_at`.

### Rhythm Elite only

Rhythm Elite (£49.99) has `max_artists = 2` — the owner plus **exactly one** shared seat. Free, Kickstart and Label Master have no shared seat.

### Undecided, and it changes the whole flow

⚠️ **Whether this invites an existing account or invites someone to register is not settled.** Label invites use `users_invitations` and invite-to-register; whether this reuses that path or gets its own is an open question.

⚠️ **What membership actually grants is also undefined** — how the member's own plan row interacts with riding the owner's Elite plan has not been decided.

⚠️ **No email template exists** for the invitation, or for "you were removed".

The `subscription_members` table is ready (`role` owner/member, `status` pending/active/removed, `invited_by`, `joined_at`, unique on `(subscription_id, user_id)`), but **nothing in the codebase reads or writes it.**

⏳ **NOT BUILT YET — returns 404 today.** Contract only. Do not build against this.

Remove the shared member from a Rhythm Elite plan.

🔑 Requires `Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}}`.

### ⚠️ The path is changing, and losing its identifier

This request is `DELETE /api/subscription/members/:reference`. The 2026-07-28 draft renames it to **`DELETE /api/subscription/members-remove`** — with **no identifier in the path at all**.

That works only while the cap is one member per plan: there is exactly one member to remove, so naming them is redundant. It stops working the moment a plan can hold more than one seat, and that is flagged as an open question.

Confirm which path wins before wiring it.

### Carry-over rule to confirm

In the earlier contract, **a member removing themselves was 403** — only the plan owner can remove. Whether that rule survives the rename is unconfirmed.

### Undecided

⚠️ What happens to the removed member's own subscription state is not defined — whether they fall back to a free row, lose access immediately, or keep it to period end.

⚠️ **No "you were removed" email template exists.**

🔑 Saved cards kept for auto-renewal, default first.

⚠️ **Currently always returns an empty list.** Nothing writes this table yet — checkout does not store a gateway card token, and `auto_renew` is 0 on every subscription. The contract is stable; data appears once off-session renewal is built.

Cards are stored as opaque gateway tokens. The token never leaves the database — the API exposes brand, last four digits and expiry only, and there is deliberately no "add card" endpoint (cards are captured by the gateway during checkout).

**200** `{payment_methods: [{id, gateway, card_brand, card_last4, card_exp_month, card_exp_year, is_default, created_at}]}`

🔑 Removes a saved card. Soft-delete — the row stays for the audit trail on past charges, but the stored token is cleared and the card drops out of the list.

`:id` is the numeric `payment_methods.id` from *List payment methods* — the one place in this API that uses a database id rather than an opaque reference.

A card belonging to someone else returns **404**, not 403: a stranger must not learn that the id exists.

**409** when the card is currently funding an active renewal — cancel the renewal or add another card first.

**200** `{status: true, message: "Payment method removed."}` · **404** not found or not yours · **409** in use for renewal.

Plans, the current subscription, upgrades, cancellation, the Rhythm Elite shared seat, and stored cards.

**Rules encoded here:** Rhythm Elite lets 2 users share one subscription — the owner invites and can remove the member; the member cannot remove themself. Expired subscriptions auto-downgrade to Free (handled by cron, not by these endpoints).

item.name: Payments

request.description:
🔑 Read-only status of a payment you own. **Never calls the gateway**, so it is cheap enough to poll on a timer while the customer is away paying.

Once the payment is confirmed, this returns the full picture — payment, active subscription and wizard state — the same shape as the verification endpoint.

**200** `{payment: {reference, status, amount, currency, amount_gbp}}` while pending; full payload once successful · **404** unknown reference, or not yours.

This does not confirm anything by itself — to actually verify and activate a charge, call `POST /api/payments/{reference}/verification`.

🔑 Call once after Flutterwave redirects the customer back (`:reference` = the checkout reference, `PAY…`).

The server re-verifies the transaction directly with Flutterwave — **the client is never trusted** — cross-checks the amount and currency against the pending order, activates the subscription, completes the onboarding wizard and queues the welcome email. Idempotent: safe to call again on an already-confirmed payment.

**200** confirmed (payment + subscription + wizard) · **202** still processing, poll `GET /api/payments/{reference}` and retry · **402** charge failed · **404** unknown/foreign reference · **409** amount mismatch, or no longer verifiable · **502** gateway unreachable.

📩 Safety net for when the customer never returns from the gateway. Note the path is **singular** — `/api/webhook/flutterwave`.

No Bearer token: authenticated by the `verif-hash` header, compared against `FLUTTERWAVE_SECRET_HASH`. Events are stored in `payment_webhooks` and deduplicated on event id, and amounts are **re-verified against the Flutterwave API** rather than trusted from the payload.

**200** received (or duplicate ignored) · **400** bad payload · **401** bad/missing signature.

Set the `flutterwave_secret_hash` collection variable before sending, or this will correctly 401.

❄️ **NOT BUILT — and not planned for this build.** Do not build against this.

📩 Gateway webhook — backend testing only. Never called by the frontend.

### Stripe is "coming soon", deliberately

Confirmed 2026-07-28: **this build is Flutterwave only.** There is no `StripeGateway` implementation. `payments.gateway` and `docs/api-endpoints.md` both mention Stripe, and `apps/Hook/Stripe/` exists as scaffolding, but nothing is wired up.

The only live webhook is **`POST /api/webhook/flutterwave`**.

### ⚠️ Note the path spelling

This request says `/api/webhooks/stripe` (plural). The implemented Flutterwave route is `/api/webhook/flutterwave` — **singular**. Which spelling becomes standard is an open question; whichever wins, this collection and the live route currently disagree.

### How the live webhook works, for reference

It sits **outside** the Bearer guard on purpose — a gateway cannot hold a user token. It authenticates on the `verif-hash` signature header, and is idempotent via a unique `(gateway, event)` constraint on `payment_webhooks`, so a replayed event cannot double-fulfil.

Fulfilment is driven by server-side verification **or** the webhook — never by the client claiming success.

🔑 Currencies the checkout accepts. `default` is always **GBP** — plan prices are stored in GBP and that never changes. The rest are what a customer may choose to be *charged* in: GBP, NGN, USD, EUR, GHS, KES, ZAR, UGX, RWF, TZS, XOF, XAF.

Use this to populate the currency selector, then price it with `GET /api/payments/convert`.

**200** `{ "default": "GBP", "currencies": ["GBP","NGN","USD", …] }`

query.description: Target currency — one of the supported codes. Required.
Plan to price. Use with billing_cycle. Omit both and send `amount` instead for a raw GBP figure.

request.description:
🔑 Server-side FX quote, so the customer sees the real figure before paying. Rates come from exchangerate-api.com and are cached for an hour.

Two ways to call it: `plan_id` + `billing_cycle` to price a plan, or a raw GBP `amount` for anything else (fast track, takedown). Returns `amount_gbp`, the `rate`, and the converted `amount` — that last figure is exactly what `POST /api/subscription/start` will charge.

**200** quote · **422** bad currency, cycle or plan · **503** FX provider unreachable.

item.description:
One payment flow for everything priced: subscription, GBP 2 extra-release fee, GBP 15 fast track, GBP 5 takedown. The triggering endpoint (plan selection, subscription order, fast-track order, submission, takedown request) answers **402** with this payload:

```json
{
  "payment_reference": "pay_2kd93a",
  "gateway": "flutterwave",
  "checkout_url": "https://checkout.flutterwave.com/...",   // Flutterwave
  "client_secret": "pi_..._secret_...",                    // Stripe instead
  "amount": "15.00", "currency": "GBP",
  "fx": {"display_amount": "28500.00", "display_currency": "NGN", "rate": "1900.00"}
}
```

**Frontend flow:** open `checkout_url` (Flutterwave) or drive Stripe.js with `client_secret` → on return, call the verification endpoint once → poll `GET /api/payments/{reference}` until `successful` or `failed`. **Fulfilment only ever happens server-side** (webhook or gateway re-verification) — the client redirect alone never unlocks anything, and amounts are re-read from the gateway, never trusted from the client.

The two webhook requests are for **backend testing only** — the frontend never calls them.

item.name: Earning

request.description:
🔑 Current wallet balance plus a summary of withdrawals still in flight (status `pending` or `processing`).

This is the "Available Funds" card and the wallet chip in the top bar.

#### Response fields

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `balance` | Spendable balance from `users_wallet`, 2 dp |
| `currency` | Always `GBP` (wallet base currency) |
| `pending_withdrawals.count` | How many withdrawal requests are not yet completed |
| `pending_withdrawals.total` | Their combined amount — already debited, so it is **not** part of `balance` |

A user with no wallet row yet gets `balance: 0` — not a 404.

#### Responses

`200` OK · `401` missing/expired token · `429` rate limited (`api_read`)

request.description:
🔑 The whole Earnings screen in one call — the headline cards plus the two *Earning History* lists. All figures are **since-joining** totals; there is no range parameter.

#### Cards → fields

| Card in the design | Field | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| Total Earning (header chip) | `total_earning` | `earnings_to_date + ongoing_earnings` — everything earned, including money still in flight |
| Available Funds | `available_funds` | Current wallet balance (same number as `GET /api/earnings`) |
| Payment Cleared | `payment_cleared` | Statement money already credited to the wallet |
| Ongoing Earnings | `ongoing_earnings` | Published statements **not yet** credited to the wallet |
| Earnings to date | `earnings_to_date` | Lifetime credits from earning sources (`royalty`, `stream_revenue`, `referral`) |
| Total Withdrawal | `total_withdrawal.count` / `.amount` | How many withdrawals completed, and their total |

#### Earning History

- `earning_history.platforms` — per-DSP totals with `logo_url` (the **Platforms** tab).
- `earning_history.royalty` — per-track totals with `isrc` (the **Royalty** tab).

Both are top 20, biggest first, summed from the statements' precomputed breakdown rows. **Empty arrays mean the empty state** ("Beginnings are so exciting!") — not an error.

#### Responses

`200` OK · `401` · `429` rate limited (`api_read`)

request.description:
🔑 One statement, owner-scoped. The `format` query parameter decides what comes back.

| `format` | Result |
|---|---|
| *(absent)* or `json` | **JSON breakdown** — statement header, per-category totals, the pre-ranked chart data and every line item. This is what the statement page renders. |
| `html` | The statement as a downloadable **HTML document** (`Content-Disposition: attachment`) |
| `csv` | The statement's **line items as CSV** |

> ⚠️ For `html` and `csv` the response is a **file, not the JSON envelope**. In Postman use **Send and Download**.

#### Path variable

- `statement_id` — the `statement_id` value from the list call (a string handle, not a numeric id).

#### JSON payload shape

- `statement` — the header: period, currency, opening/closing balance, gross, deductions, tax, `net_amount_due`, `wallet_credited`.
- `categories[]` — per-category totals (`category`, `units`, `amount`), already in display order.
- `overview` — **precomputed chart data**, keyed `country` / `dsp` / `track` / `contract`. Each row has `rank`, `name`, `amount`, `units`, `percentage`, plus `country_code`, `logo_url` or `isrc` where relevant. Render these directly — do not re-aggregate the line items.
- `line_items[]` — the full per-track × platform × country rows behind the totals.

#### Responses

`200` OK (JSON, or a file when `format=html|csv`) · `401` · `404` unknown id, not yours, or not published · `422` bad `format` · `429` (`api_read`)

request.description:
🔑 Wallet transaction history, newest first — with the filter chips from the transactions screen.

#### Filters (all optional, combine with AND)

| Param | Values |
|---|---|
| `type` | `credit` · `debit` |
| `source` | `royalty` · `stream_revenue` · `referral` · `deposit` · `refund` · `withdrawal` · `takedown_fee` · `release_fee` · `fast_track_fee` · `subscription` · `payout` · `adjustment` |
| `from` | Start date `YYYY-MM-DD`, inclusive |
| `to` | End date `YYYY-MM-DD`, inclusive |

The **export** request accepts exactly the same four — build the query once and reuse it.

Anything outside these enums, a malformed date, or `from` later than `to` returns `422` with the offending field in `errors`. The filters that were actually applied are echoed back in `meta.filters`.

#### Response fields

`reference` is the public handle — use it for the details and report calls, never a numeric id. `balance_before` / `balance_after` let you show the running balance without recomputing it.

request.description:
🔑 Flag a problem transaction to support — the **Report Transaction** popup.

#### Path variable

- `reference` — the transaction's public reference.

#### Body

| Field | Rules |
|---|---|
| `description` | **Required.** 1–2000 characters. The free-text "Describe the issue" field. |

The popup also shows a *Transaction Reference ID* input; that value is the `:reference` in the URL, so it does not go in the body.

#### Behaviour

One report per transaction. Repeating the call returns `409` no matter what state the existing report is in. A new report starts as `open`; support moves it to `resolved` or `dismissed` later.

#### Responses

`201` created · `401` · `404` unknown reference or not yours · `409` already reported · `422` empty or over-long description (detail in `errors.description`) · `429` (`api_write`)

item.description:
Wallet, revenue statements and transaction history — the Earnings screen (`/api/earnings*`).

All routes need the collection Bearer token (`{{access_token}}`, auto-filled by **Auth › Login**). Scope is strictly the signed-in user's own wallet for every account type; label roster money lives under Label/Withdrawals. Read-mostly: the only write here is reporting a transaction.

**Notes for the frontend**

- Amounts are **numbers** rounded to 2 dp (not strings). Wallet base currency is `GBP`.
- Lists paginate with `?page=&limit=` (`limit` clamped to 100) and return `meta.pagination`.
- Timestamps are `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` (server time) unless noted.
- Two endpoints return **files, not JSON**: the statement download (`?format=html|csv`) and the transaction export. Use *Send and Download* in Postman.
- The old `/api/wallet*` paths are gone — everything moved under `/api/earnings*`.

request.description:
Add a bank account (max **5** per user). The first account automatically becomes the default; later ones only when `is_default: true` is sent — the previous default is unset in the same transaction, so there is always exactly one. Triggers the "bank details updated" security email.

**Auth:** Bearer token (collection-level).

| Body field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `account_name` | string | yes | Name on the account, 2–150 chars |
| `bank_name` | string | yes | 2–255 chars |
| `account_number` | string | yes | 4–50 letters/digits |
| `bank_country` | string | no | Two-letter code, e.g. `NG`, `GB` |
| `bank_code` | string | for NG | Must match a code from `GET /api/meta/banks?country=NG` |
| `routing_number` | string | no | Max 50 chars |
| `iban` | string | no | Max 50 chars |
| `swift_code` | string | no | Max 20 chars |
| `currency` | string | no | Defaults to `ngn` for NG, `gbp` otherwise |
| `is_default` | bool | no | Make this the default payout account |

**Statuses:** `201` created · `409` duplicate account, or the 5-account limit is reached · `422` validation failed (`errors` map names the field) · `401` · `429` (`api_write`).

request.description:
Start a withdrawal. Creates a `pending` request and emails a 6-digit OTP that expires in **15 minutes**.

**The wallet is NOT debited here** — the money stays spendable until the OTP is confirmed. So a user who abandons this step never has funds stuck in limbo.

One open request per user: starting a new one silently cancels and replaces the previous unconfirmed one, and a fresh OTP is sent (older codes stop working).

**Auth:** Bearer token (collection-level).

| Body field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `amount` | number | yes | GBP, greater than 0, max 2 decimal places |
| `bank_id` | int | no | Account to pay to; falls back to the default account |

The balance and daily-limit checks here are a courtesy so the user hears "no" before an OTP round-trip — the checks that actually gate the money run again at confirm.

request.description:
Confirm the open withdrawal with the emailed 6-digit code. **No reference in the path or body** — a user has only one open request, so the code alone identifies it.

**This is where the wallet is debited.** In one transaction the balance and daily limit are re-checked under a row lock, the money is taken, the ledger entry is written, and the request becomes `processing` — queued for the monthly payout run. The "request received" email goes out with the payout date.

The OTP is single-use. A wrong or expired code returns `422`; start the withdrawal again to get a fresh one.

**Auth:** Bearer token (collection-level).

| Body field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `otp` | string | yes | The 6-digit code from the email |

The `200` response returns the new wallet balance, so the UI can update the balance without a second call.

**Statuses:** `200` confirmed, wallet debited · `422` wrong or expired code · `404` no request waiting to be confirmed · `409` balance changed, daily limit passed, or already confirmed/cancelled · `403` wallet is label-managed · `401` · `429` (OTP attempts are limited tightly — 3/min per account).

item.description:
Saved bank accounts and OTP-confirmed withdrawals from the artist wallet. All routes need the collection-level Bearer token.

**Withdrawal flow — money moves at confirm, not at request:**

1. `POST /api/withdrawals/request` — checks balance and the GBP 1,000/day limit, creates a `pending` request and emails a 6-digit OTP (15-minute expiry). **Nothing is debited yet.** A user has one open request at a time — starting a new one replaces the old.
2. `POST /api/withdrawals/request-confirm` — send just the OTP (no reference needed: only one request can be open). **The wallet is debited here** and the request becomes `processing`.
3. `POST /api/withdrawals/request/{reference}` — cancels a request that is still `pending`. Nothing to refund, because nothing was debited.

Confirmed requests are paid in the monthly payout run (the **25th**). The confirm response returns `expected_payout_date` so the UI can tell the user when.

**Status lifecycle:** `pending` (awaiting OTP) → `processing` (confirmed, queued for payout) → `completed` | `failed`. `cancelled` means the user cancelled it, or it was replaced by a newer request.

**Bank accounts:** max **5** per user, exactly one is the default. Nigerian accounts must send a `bank_code` from `GET /api/meta/banks?country=NG`; other countries are free-text. Adding or removing an account sends a security email.

Artists signed to a label that fully controls wallets get `403` on request/confirm — their money moves via label payouts (separate module, not built yet).

item.name: Analytics

query.description: One of `7d, 14d, 30d, 60d, 120d, 180d, 1yr`. Defaults to `30d` if omitted. NOTE: `all-time` is NOT accepted here (422) — it is valid on the other four Analytics endpoints.

request.description:
🔑 Everything on the top half of the Trends & Analytics screen: the headline cards, the release status chips, and the Earnings History panel.

### Range

`?range=` accepts **`7d, 14d, 30d, 60d, 120d, 180d, 1yr`**. Omitted → `30d`.

**This endpoint does not accept** **`all-time`** (the other four do) — headline cards always show a bounded window. Sending it returns `422`:

``` json
{ "status": false, "message": "Invalid range.",
  "errors": { "range": "Range must be one of: 7d, 14d, 30d, 60d, 120d, 180d, 1yr." } }

 ```

The window is inclusive and ends today: `7d` = today plus the six days before it. `meta.from` / `meta.to` tell you exactly what was measured.

### Response

``` json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Analytics overview.",
  "data": {
    "streams":   { "lifetime": 192463897, "range": 874376 },
    "downloads": { "lifetime": 12045,     "range": 318 },
    "artists":   { "lifetime": 12,        "range": 8 },
    "releases":  { "total": 24, "approved": 18, "rejected": 3, "pending": 3 },
    "revenue":   { "total": 2384.00, "currency": "GBP" },
    "earnings_history": [
      { "platform": "Apple Music",  "amount": 757.15, "share": 31.76 },
      { "platform": "Spotify",      "amount": 657.29, "share": 27.57 }
    ]
  },
  "meta": {
    "range": "30d",
    "from": "2026-06-30",
    "to": "2026-07-29",
    "last_synced_at": "2026-07-27 04:15:22"
  }
}

 ```

### Field notes

- **`lifetime`** **vs** **`range`** — `lifetime` ignores the window entirely (all data we hold); `range` is the window. The big number on each card is `lifetime`, the small one under it is `range`.
    
- **`artists`** counts artists that **actually had streams**, not roster size. For a solo artist account this is `1` (or `0` in a window with no streams) — it is meaningful for labels.
    
- **`releases.pending`** folds the `pending_review` status. Counts are lifetime, not windowed.
    
- **`revenue.total`** is the sum of `earnings_history`, so the panel and the card can never disagree.
    
- **`earnings_history`** is sorted highest-earning first. `share` is that DSP's percentage of `revenue.total`, recomputed over the window.
    

### Revenue is monthly-grain — read this

Revenue comes from published **monthly statements**, not from the daily stream rows. A `7d` or `14d` range will usually match no statement at all and correctly returns `"total": 0` with an empty `earnings_history`.

**That is not an error state — do not render it as one.** Use `30d` or wider for anything money-related.

### `meta.last_synced_at`

When the stream sync last completed for this account (`null` if it never has). Sync is **weekly by default**, so numbers legitimately lag by days. Render this as "as of …" so a stale-looking dashboard doesn't read as broken.

### Who sees what

| Account type | Sees |
| --- | --- |
| `artist` | Their own artists |
| `label` | The whole roster, aggregated |
| `label_member` | The roster — **only** with the `analytics.view` permission, else `403` |
| `contributor` | Nothing — a valid `200` response of zeroes |

Scope is always derived from your token. There is no `?artist=` parameter; you cannot request someone else's numbers.

### Responses

`200` OK · `403` label staff without `analytics.view` · `422` invalid range

query.description: Optional. A DSP name or slug (e.g. `spotify`, `Apple Music`) — narrows the series to that one platform. Case-insensitive. Use the `platform` or `slug` value from Platform breakdown.

request.description:
🔑 The daily series behind the main chart — and, with `?platform=`, behind each "Growth by platform" card's sparkline.

**Replaces the old `?from=&to=` date window.** There is no free date picker; use the fixed `?range=` enum below.

### Range

`?range=` accepts **`7d, 14d, 30d, 60d, 120d, 180d, 1yr, all-time`**. Omitted → `30d`. Anything else → `422`.

`all-time` drops the date filter — it means "since we started counting", i.e. as far back as the stream sync has run, not the artist's whole career.

### `?platform=` — the per-DSP sparkline

Without it, the series covers **all** platforms. With it, the series is that one DSP only.

Each "Growth by platform" card has its own range dropdown, so it is **one call per card**:

```
GET /api/analytics/streams?range=1yr&platform=spotify
```

Matching is case-insensitive and accepts either the display name or the slug. An unknown platform is **not** an error — you get a valid `200` with an empty `series` and zero totals. Pass the `platform` or `slug` value straight from the Platform breakdown response and it will always match.

### Response

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Streams breakdown.",
  "data": {
    "series": [
      { "date": "2026-07-01", "streams": 5231, "downloads": 12 },
      { "date": "2026-07-02", "streams": 4884, "downloads": 9 }
    ],
    "totals": { "streams": 874376, "downloads": 318 }
  },
  "meta": {
    "range": "30d",
    "from": "2026-06-30",
    "to": "2026-07-29",
    "last_synced_at": "2026-07-27 04:15:22",
    "platform": null
  }
}
```

### Field notes

- **`series` is sparse.** Days with no streams are **absent**, not zero-filled. To draw a continuous axis, generate the dates from `meta.from`/`meta.to` and left-join the series onto them — otherwise gaps will render as if the line jumped.
- `series` is ascending by `date` (`YYYY-MM-DD`).
- `totals` is the sum of the returned series, so it always matches the chart you drew.
- `meta.platform` echoes back what you filtered on (`null` when unfiltered) — useful for keeping card state in sync.
- Series length is bounded by the range: `1yr` returns up to 365 points, `all-time` as many days as exist.

### Responses

`200` OK · `403` label staff without `analytics.view` · `422` invalid range

🔑 Stream totals per DSP, biggest first — the "Growth by platform" cards. **Counts only, no money.** Per-DSP earnings live on **Analytics › Overview** (`earnings_history`), because revenue is only available at monthly-statement grain, not per stream row. ### Range `?range=` accepts **`7d, 14d, 30d, 60d, 120d, 180d, 1yr, all-time`**. Omitted → `30d`. ### Response ```json { "status": true, "message": "Platform breakdown.", "data": { "platforms": [ { "platform": "Spotify", "slug": "spotify", "logo_url": "https://api.example.com/assets/dsp/spotify.svg", "streams": 1147113, "downloads": 0, "share": 83.72 }, { "platform": "Apple Music", "slug": "apple-music", "logo_url": "https://api.example.com/assets/dsp/itunes.svg", "streams": 214116, "downloads": 0, "share": 15.63 } ], "totals": { "streams": 1370229, "downloads": 0 } }, "meta": { "range": "30d", "from": "2026-06-30", "to": "2026-07-29", "last_synced_at": "2026-07-27 04:15:22" } } ``` ### Field notes - **`platform`** is the display name, ready to render. Use it for labels. - **`slug`** is the stable machine key — use it for React keys, icon lookups, and to pass into **Streams time series** `?platform=`. Can be `null` for a DSP we have not catalogued yet. - **`logo_url`** is a **fully-qualified URL**, or `null` when we have no artwork for that DSP. Always null-check before rendering an ``; fall back to the platform's first letter or a generic mark. - **`share`** is that DSP's percentage of `totals.streams`, 2dp. Shares sum to ~100 (rounding aside). - Sorted by `streams` descending. The array holds **every** DSP with streams in the window — take the first N for the cards. - An empty `platforms` array with zero totals is a legitimate "no streams in this window" answer, not an error. ### Responses `200` OK · `403` label staff without `analytics.view` · `422` invalid range

🔑 Per-country streams, share and revenue — the "World Domination" map.

> **Path is `/countries` (plural).** Earlier drafts said `/country`; that singular form does not exist.

### Range

`?range=` accepts **`7d, 14d, 30d, 60d, 120d, 180d, 1yr, all-time`**. Omitted → `30d`.

### Response

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Country breakdown.",
  "data": {
    "countries": [
      { "code": "US", "name": "United States",  "streams": 421338, "downloads": 120, "revenue": 119.83, "share": 48.19 },
      { "code": "NG", "name": "Nigeria",        "streams": 198442, "downloads": 64,  "revenue": 29.47,  "share": 22.70 },
      { "code": "GB", "name": "United Kingdom", "streams": 96110,  "downloads": 31,  "revenue": 21.51,  "share": 10.99 }
    ],
    "totals": { "streams": 874376, "downloads": 318, "revenue": 191.71, "currency": "GBP" }
  },
  "meta": {
    "range": "30d",
    "from": "2026-06-30",
    "to": "2026-07-29",
    "last_synced_at": "2026-07-27 04:15:22"
  }
}
```

### Field notes

- **`code`** is ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, uppercase — the key to join against your map's geography.
- **`name`** is the English display name. For an unrecognised code, `name` falls back to the code itself, so it is never `null`.
- **`share`** is the percentage of `totals.streams` (**not** of revenue), 2dp — that is what shades the map.
- Sorted by `streams` descending, then `revenue`.

### Two different sources — the important bit

`streams` / `downloads` / `share` come from the **daily stream rows**. `revenue` comes from the **monthly revenue statements**. They are joined by country, but they do not move together:

- A country can have **streams but `revenue: 0`** — normal for short ranges, since no monthly statement falls inside the window.
- A country can appear with **`streams: 0, share: 0` but non-zero `revenue`** — it earned in a statement covering this window but has no daily stream rows for it. **These rows are still in the array.** If you shade purely by `share`, they render invisible while still contributing to `totals.revenue`, which looks like the numbers don't add up. Decide deliberately whether to plot or filter them.

`totals.revenue` is the sum of all `revenue` values; `totals.currency` is the statement currency (`GBP` when there is nothing to report).

### Responses

`200` OK · `403` label staff without `analytics.view` · `422` invalid range

request.description:
🔑 Top tracks by streams for the window, paginated.

> **Pagination uses `limit`, not `size`.** The Analytics folder uses `?page=&limit=`. Default `limit` is 20, silently clamped to a max of 100 (asking for 999 gives you 100 — check `meta.pagination.limit` for what you actually got).

### Range

`?range=` accepts **`7d, 14d, 30d, 60d, 120d, 180d, 1yr, all-time`**. Omitted → `30d`.

### Response

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Top tracks.",
  "data": {
    "tracks": [
      {
        "reference": "snh9vizmfzs1zqv",
        "title": "FOR ME",
        "isrc": "QZN882401757",
        "release_title": "FOR ME",
        "release_type": "single",
        "cover": "cover-67442a8246717.png",
        "streams": 49469,
        "downloads": 0,
        "share": 57.85
      }
    ]
  },
  "meta": {
    "range": "30d",
    "from": "2026-06-30",
    "to": "2026-07-29",
    "last_synced_at": "2026-07-27 04:15:22",
    "pagination": {
      "page": 1, "limit": 20, "total": 137, "pages": 7,
      "has_next": true, "has_prev": false
    }
  }
}
```

### Field notes

- **`share` is stable across pages.** It is the track's percentage of the **whole window's** streams, not of the current page — so a track shows the same percentage on page 1 and page 7, and shares across all pages sum to ~100.
- **`reference`** is the track's opaque public id — use it for row keys and for linking into the release.
- **`release_type`** is one of `single`, `ep`, `album`, `compilation`. Pair it with `release_title` to render "Single: FOR ME", as the Earnings History panel does.
- **`cover`** is a **bare filename**, not a URL — unlike `logo_url` on Platform breakdown. The public path prefix is owned by the Releases section, which is not built yet, so **do not hard-code a prefix**; treat this field as unstable and confirm before wiring it up.
- **Nullable fields:** `title`, `isrc`, `release_title`, `release_type` and `cover` can all be `null`. A track with streams whose release row has since been removed still appears (so the totals stay honest) but carries no metadata. Guard every one of these before rendering.
- Sorted by `streams` descending, with a stable tiebreak, so paging never repeats or drops a row.

### Responses

`200` OK · `403` label staff without `analytics.view` · `422` invalid range

item.name: Notifications

request.description:
✅ **Live** — implemented and verified 2026-07-28.

The in-app Notification Center. Newest first.

🔑 Requires `Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}}`. Rows are scoped to the token's user.

### ⚠️ Pagination is `limit`, not `size`

This endpoint uses **`?limit=`**. Other lists in this collection say `size` — Notifications settled on `limit`. Default 20, capped at 100. `page` is 1-based.

### 200 response

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Notifications.",
  "data": {
    "notifications": [
      {
        "reference": "NOTIF003",
        "title": "Statement ready",
        "message": "June statement is published.",
        "is_read": false,
        "read_at": null,
        "created_at": "2026-07-28 17:23:33"
      }
    ]
  },
  "meta": {
    "unread_count": 3,
    "pagination": {
      "page": 1,
      "limit": 20,
      "total": 3,
      "pages": 1,
      "has_next": false,
      "has_prev": false
    }
  }
}
```

### `meta.unread_count` is the bell badge

Read it from here. There is **no separate count endpoint** — that was deliberate. It is also returned by both mark-read endpoints, so you never need to re-fetch the list just to refresh the badge.

### ⚠️ Notifications are not tappable

`users_notification` holds **`title` + `message` only** — no `type`, no link or action URL, no actor. So rows cannot deep-link ("Your release was approved →" opening that release), and there are no per-type icons.

If the Figma Notification Center expects either, that needs new columns and owner approval. Do not design rows around data that isn't there.

### Also worth knowing

**Nothing writes this table yet.** These endpoints read and update it, but no producer exists — Releases, Earning, Withdrawals and Label invites are all future writers. Expect the list to be empty until those ship.

There is **no delete endpoint**, deliberately. Rows accumulate; there is no per-row dismiss.

`reference` (varchar 25) is the public handle. The numeric `notify_id` is never exposed.

✅ **Live** — implemented and verified 2026-07-28.

Mark one notification as read.

🔑 Requires `Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}}`. No body.

### ⚠️ The verb changed: `PATCH` → `POST`

This request was `PATCH` in the earlier contract. **It is now `POST`** — that was the decision. `PATCH` will 404.

### `:reference` is the public handle

Use `reference` from the list response (varchar 25) — e.g. `NOTIF003`. The numeric `notify_id` is never exposed.

⚠️ The route pattern is **alphanumeric only**, deliberately, so `read-all` can never be swallowed as a reference.

### Idempotent — call it freely

Marking an already-read notification again returns **200**, not an error. You do not need to check `is_read` first.

Better still: `read_at` is stamped **only on the first transition**, so it keeps meaning "when they actually read it" rather than "when they last tapped it" — re-marking does not overwrite the original timestamp. Verified.

### 200 response

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Notification marked as read.",
  "meta": { "unread_count": 2 }
}
```

`meta.unread_count` is the fresh badge value — update the bell from this rather than re-fetching the list.

**404** — the reference does not exist **or is not yours**. Deliberately the same answer, so this cannot be used to probe which references are real.

✅ **Live** — implemented and verified 2026-07-28.

Mark every unread notification as read — the "Mark all as read" action.

🔑 Requires `Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}}`. No body.

One UPDATE, so every row marked in this call shares the same `read_at` stamp. **Already-read rows are left untouched** and keep their original timestamps.

### 200 response

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "All notifications marked as read.",
  "data": { "marked": 2 },
  "meta": { "unread_count": 0 }
}
```

`marked` is how many rows actually changed — `0` when there was nothing unread, which is still a 200, not an error.

`meta.unread_count` is always `0` after this. Update the bell from it rather than re-fetching the list.

ℹ️ Route ordering: this is registered **before** `/{reference}`, and the reference pattern excludes hyphens, so `read-all` can never be mistaken for a notification reference.
