Global search modal — `?q=` returns grouped results across releases, tracks and artists.

🔑 Requires `Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}}`.

⚠️ **Scoped to what you own.** Search never reaches another user's catalogue.

### This one has the least definition in the whole collection

Unlike every other section, **Search has no design document** — there is no `tasks/12-search.md`. The only specification anywhere is a single line in `docs/api-endpoints.md`: *"Global search modal: `?q=` → grouped releases/tracks/artists (own scope only)."*

Nothing else is settled. All of the following are undefined:

- the response shape and how groups are keyed
- whether results paginate, and under which param
- minimum query length, and what an empty or 1-character `q` returns
- whether it searches titles only, or also artist names, ISRC, UPC
- result limits per group
- whether label accounts search their whole roster

**Do not design a UI against assumptions here.** If the search modal is on your roadmap, this section needs a spec written first — flag it and I'll work through it properly.

item.name: Meta

request.description:
🔑 **Requires a token.** Every `/api/meta/*` list is authenticated — earlier drafts marked this one public, it is not.

47 top-level genres, each carrying its own sub-genres (429 rows in total). The release form is a two-step select, so the nesting is done server-side — you never have to regroup a flat list.

### Response

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Genres retrieved.",
  "data": {
    "genres": [
      { "slug": "african", "name": "African",
        "sub_genres": [ { "slug": "afrobeats", "name": "Afrobeats" } ] },
      { "slug": "alternative", "name": "Alternative", "sub_genres": [] }
    ]
  }
}
```

- **Store the `slug`, never the name.** `releases.genre` and `releases.sub_genre` are slug columns.
- `sub_genres` may be an empty array — a top-level genre is a valid choice on its own.
- Order is curated (`sort_order`), not alphabetical. Render it as given.

### Caching (applies to every Meta endpoint)

Responses carry an `ETag` and `Cache-Control: private, max-age=86400`. Send the tag back as `If-None-Match` and you get an empty **`304`** instead of the full payload:

```
If-None-Match: "a3f1…"
```

The ETag is derived from the payload, so it changes exactly when the data does. Cache these lists on the client and revalidate — do not refetch them on every screen.

### Responses

`200` OK · `304` your cached copy is current · `500` the list could not be loaded (never an empty dropdown)

🔑 **Requires a token.**

193 metadata languages for the release and track forms.

### Response

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Languages retrieved.",
  "data": {
    "languages": [
      { "slug": "english", "name": "English", "code": "en", "is_metadata_language": true },
      { "slug": "instrumental", "name": "Instrumental", "code": "zxx", "is_metadata_language": false }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Field notes

- **Store the `slug`.** `releases.language` and `release_tracks.language` are slug columns. `code` is for display/ISO interop only.
- **`code` is NOT unique** — Revelator maps both Hindi and Bihari to `hi`. Never key a dropdown or a map by `code`; use `slug`.
- **`is_metadata_language` is `false` for exactly one entry:** *Instrumental* (`zxx`, the ISO code for "no linguistic content"). It is returned rather than filtered out because a track with no lyrics is a real case. **Your form decides** whether to offer it — typically yes for a track's audio language, no for the release's metadata language.

### Caching

`ETag` + `Cache-Control: private, max-age=86400`. Send `If-None-Match` to get a `304`.

### Responses

`200` OK · `304` cached copy current · `500` list could not be loaded

🔑 **Requires a token.** The **33 pickable stores** a release can be delivered to — the DSP checklist on the release form. > This is the *pickable* list only (`is_active` **and** `is_display`). The full `streaming_platforms` table holds 540+ rows, including delivery partners an artist never chooses (The Orchard, FUGA) and reporting-only rows that exist so synced data resolves. Those are deliberately not returned here. ### Response ```json { "status": true, "message": "Platforms retrieved.", "data": { "platforms": [ { "id": 9, "slug": "spotify", "name": "Spotify", "logo_url": "https://api.example.com/assets/dsp/spotify.svg", "supports_videos": false, "delivery_lead_days": 5, "takedown_lead_days": 3 } ] } } ``` ### Field notes - **`id` is the one place in Meta that matters more than `slug`** — `release_platforms.platform_id` stores this integer. Send `id` back when selecting DSPs; everything else in Meta is keyed by slug. - **`logo_url`** is a fully-qualified URL, or `null` when we hold no artwork for that DSP. Null-check before rendering an ``. - **`delivery_lead_days` / `takedown_lead_days`** are nullable — use them to show "live in ~5 days", and hide the estimate entirely when null rather than printing "null days". - **`supports_videos`** gates whether a video release may target this store. - Order is curated (`sort_order`). ### Related **Analytics › Platform breakdown** returns a different shape (`platform`, `slug`, `logo_url`, stream counts) and covers DSPs that *reported streams*, which is not the same set as the pickable list here. Do not treat the two as interchangeable. ### Caching `ETag` + `Cache-Control: private, max-age=86400`. Send `If-None-Match` to get a `304`. ### Responses `200` OK · `304` cached copy current · `500` list could not be loaded

query.description: Two-letter ISO country code, uppercased server-side. Defaults to `NG` if omitted. **Only `NG` is supported today** — any other valid code returns 422.

request.description:
🔑 **Requires a token.**

124 active Nigerian banks for the withdrawal-account form.

### `?country=`

Defaults to `NG` if omitted. Case-insensitive.

**Only `NG` is supported today.** Any other country returns **`422`** — deliberately, rather than an empty list, because an empty dropdown reads to the user as "no banks exist":

```json
{ "status": false, "message": "Validation failed.",
  "errors": { "country": "Bank lists are only available for: NG." } }
```

A malformed code (not two letters) also `422`s, with a different message:

```json
{ "errors": { "country": "Must be a two-letter country code, e.g. NG." } }
```

Render `errors.country` directly — both messages are written to be shown to the user.

### Response

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Banks retrieved.",
  "data": {
    "country": "NG",
    "banks": [
      {
        "code": "120001",
        "name": "9mobile 9Payment Service Bank",
        "slug": "9mobile-9payment-service-bank-ng",
        "type": "nuban",
        "currency": "NGN"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Field notes

- **`code` is what you submit** when adding a withdrawal account (Paystack's bank code) — not `slug`, not `id`.
- **`code` is a string, not a number.** Leading zeros are significant; parsing it as an integer will corrupt it.
- `data.country` echoes the resolved country, so you can confirm what the defaulting did.
- Inactive and deleted banks are filtered out server-side — everything returned is selectable.
- `type` is the account-number scheme (`nuban`); `currency` is always `NGN` for this list.

### Caching

`ETag` + `Cache-Control: private, max-age=86400`. Send `If-None-Match` to get a `304`. The ETag covers the response body, so `?country=` variants tag separately.

### Responses

`200` OK · `304` cached copy current · `422` unsupported or malformed country · `500` list could not be loaded

🔑 **Requires a token.**

410 credit **roles**, returned in 4 groups — the credits picker on the track form.

> These are *roles* ("Producer", "Lead Vocals"), **not people**. The people are release contributors, set via **Releases › Set track contributors**.

### Response

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Contributor roles retrieved.",
  "data": {
    "groups": [
      { "group": "artist_credit", "label": "Artist credits",
        "roles": [ { "slug": "primary-artist", "name": "Primary Artist" } ] },
      { "group": "writing",     "label": "Writing & composition",    "roles": [] },
      { "group": "production",  "label": "Production & engineering",  "roles": [] },
      { "group": "performance", "label": "Performers & instruments",  "roles": [] }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Why grouping matters

The four groups always come back in this fixed order, and it is deliberate — the sizes are wildly uneven:

| group | label | roles |
|---|---|---|
| `artist_credit` | Artist credits | 4 |
| `writing` | Writing & composition | 10 |
| `production` | Production & engineering | 27 |
| `performance` | Performers & instruments | **369** |

Render the groups in the order given. If you flatten or alphabetise, the 4 credits nearly every release needs get buried under 369 instruments.

- **Store the `slug`** — `release_contributors.role` is a slug column.
- `roles` can be an empty array for a group; render the group header only if it has roles.

### Caching

`ETag` + `Cache-Control: private, max-age=86400`. Send `If-None-Match` to get a `304`.

### Responses

`200` OK · `304` cached copy current · `500` list could not be loaded

🔑 **Requires a token.**

28 version labels — Radio Edit, Single Version, Album Version, Remix, Live, and the rest.

Note the path is **`/release-versions`** (hyphenated).

### Response

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Release versions retrieved.",
  "data": {
    "versions": [
      { "slug": "radio-edit",     "name": "Radio Edit" },
      { "slug": "single-version", "name": "Single Version" },
      { "slug": "album-version",  "name": "Album Version" }
    ]
  }
}
```

- **Store the `slug`** — `release_tracks.version` and `releases.version` are slug columns.
- Both fields are **optional**: a track with no version variant stores `null`. Do not force a selection.
- Order is curated (`sort_order`), most-used first.

### Caching

`ETag` + `Cache-Control: private, max-age=86400`. Send `If-None-Match` to get a `304`.

### Responses

`200` OK · `304` cached copy current · `500` list could not be loaded

🔑 **Requires a token.**

134 timezone options for the Language & Region screen.

### Response

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Timezones retrieved.",
  "data": {
    "timezones": [
      { "slug": "international-date-line-west", "label": "International Date Line West" }
    ]
  }
}
```

### ⚠️ Display only — do not compute time with these

`slug` is what `users.timezone` stores, and `label` is what you show. **Neither carries a UTC offset or an IANA identifier** (`Africa/Lagos`), so nothing can convert a timestamp using this list.

- Do **not** feed `slug` to `Intl.DateTimeFormat`, `date-fns-tz`, Luxon, or any tz library — it will not resolve.
- To render times in the user's local zone, use the **browser's** zone (`Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone`), not this field.
- All API timestamps are already ISO-8601 UTC.

Mapping these slugs to real IANA zones is a known open item; treat the field as a label until that lands.

### Caching

`ETag` + `Cache-Control: private, max-age=86400`. Send `If-None-Match` to get a `304`.

### Responses

`200` OK · `304` cached copy current · `500` list could not be loaded

🔑 **Requires a token.**

251 countries — ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, each with its default currency and dial code. Feeds the address, phone and withdrawal forms.

### Response

```json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Countries retrieved.",
  "data": {
    "countries": [
      { "code": "AD", "name": "Andorra",  "currency": "EUR", "dial": "+376" },
      { "code": "NG", "name": "Nigeria",  "currency": "NGN", "dial": "+234" }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Field notes

- **`code`** is the uppercase alpha-2 stored in `users.country`, and the key to join against **Analytics › Country breakdown**, which returns the same codes.
- **`dial`** already includes the `+`. Do not prepend another one.
- **`currency`** is the country's *default* — a convenience for pre-selecting a currency, not an authoritative statement about what we can pay out in. For withdrawals, the supported set is decided by **Meta › Banks** and the Withdrawals folder.
- Sorted alphabetically by `name`.

### Caching

`ETag` + `Cache-Control: private, max-age=86400`. Send `If-None-Match` to get a `304`.

### Responses

`200` OK · `304` cached copy current · `500` list could not be loaded

Proxy search against Apple Music — the sibling of the Spotify lookup, for the same "does this artist already exist?" step in the release wizard.

🔑 Requires `Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}}`.

### Why it isn't live

The other 8 Meta endpoints serve **local reference data** and are built. These two artist-lookup requests are **outbound third-party proxies** and are not.

### ⚠️ It may not stay in Meta

Same open question as the Spotify lookup: keep it here, or move it to Releases where the picker lives? **The path may change — confirm before wiring.**

### Undefined

Credentials, rate limits, caching, pagination and response shape are all unsettled. Apple Music's API needs a signed developer token, which does not exist in this codebase.

See also: `POST /api/me/artist/profile` in the Account folder, which stores the resulting `apple_music_url`. **That endpoint is live** and accepts any valid URL independently of this lookup.

⏳ **NOT BUILT YET — returns 404 today.** Contract only. Do not build against this.

Proxy search against Spotify — powers the "does this artist already exist on Spotify?" step in the release wizard, so a release can be attached to the right artist profile rather than creating a duplicate.

🔑 Requires `Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}}`.

### Why it isn't live

The other 8 Meta endpoints (genres, languages, platforms, contributors, release-versions, timezones, countries, banks) are **built and serve local reference data**. These two artist-lookup requests are different in kind: they are **outbound proxies to a third party**, and neither is implemented.

### ⚠️ It may not stay in Meta

Open question: keep artist lookup in Meta, or move it to Releases where the picker actually lives? Meta is otherwise "static reference data we own" — a live third-party search sits oddly beside it. **The path may change to `/api/releases/...` — confirm before wiring.**

### Undefined

Nothing is settled about credentials handling, rate limits, result caching, pagination, or the response shape. Spotify's API requires app credentials and enforces its own rate limits — none of that plumbing exists.

See also: `POST /api/me/artist/profile` in the Account folder, which stores the resulting `spotify_url` on the artist profile. **That endpoint is live** and takes any valid URL — it does not depend on this lookup.
